a20.speaker: Maryan Jeylani Maye, IDP mother of seven in a Mogadishu displacement camp
a20.name: Maryan Jeylani Maye
a20.title: IDP mother of seven in a Mogadishu displacement camp
a20.speech: Says she was kidnapped, forced into a vehicle, and threatened with the loss of food assistance if she did not register and have her photo taken. "They told us we should register in order to receive food." ; "After they took our photos and names, they said it's for a vote—and that we must vote for Hassan Sheikh Mohamud." ; Described the entire operation as a deceitful tactic that preyed on vulnerable people through false promises of aid: "It's a trap. They used food to manipulate us."

a20.speaker: Saido Mohamud, IDP woman
a20.name: Saido Mohamud
a20.title: IDP woman
a20.speech: Said they were promised $25 in mobile money after registering but received nothing, adding that the middleman in charge allegedly stole the money. "They told us we'd get $25 via EVC if we registered, but we went home empty-handed."

a20.speaker: Danish Refugee Council (report cited)
a20.name: Danish Refugee Council (report cited)
a20.speech: Approximately 84% of Somalia's IDPs live in urban areas, with Mogadishu alone hosting between 400,000 and 518,000 people.

a20.speaker: University administrators in Mogadishu
a20.name: University administrators in Mogadishu
a20.speech: Say they have received threats from the electoral commission, warning that institutions refusing to register students, lecturers, and staff will face punitive action, including closure and the use of security forces.

a20.speaker: Abdirahman Abdishakur Warsame, Opposition MP
a20.name: Abdirahman Abdishakur Warsame
a20.title: Opposition MP
a20.speech: Condemned the reports, calling the commission's actions "disgraceful" and "illegitimate." In a statement posted to social media, he wrote: "We strongly condemn the disgraceful act by the one-sided electoral committee pressuring universities in the capital to forcibly register students, lecturers, and university staff. The committee has threatened any university that refuses to comply with their decision, warning that they will take action against them using security forces."

a180.speaker: Sophie (not her real name), mother of a malnourished one-year-old and beneficiary of US food support
a180.name: Sophie (not her real name)
a180.title: mother of a malnourished one-year-old and beneficiary of US food support
a180.speech: "My daughter was very sickly and had diarrhoea, so I took her to the clinic for a consultation. I had no idea that the problem was malnutrition" ; "The treatment is going very well, and her weight has increased to above 9kg by August" ; "When we started with RUTF, my daughter didn't take it well. I mixed it with porridge, and she became receptive to it, and now enjoys eating it. Thank you for helping Namibia with this life-saving product."

a180.speaker: Sophie (not her real name), beneficiary
a180.name: Sophie (not her real name)
a180.title: beneficiary
a180.speech: According to Sophie, having a sickly infant and not knowing what the problem is, is the most daunting thing a parent can go through, and not having the ability to afford healthcare is an even bigger problem.

a180.speaker: //Kharas regional health directorate
a180.name: //Kharas regional health directorate
a180.speech: Confirmed that malnutrition in children under five years is primarily manifested through diarrhoea, which is how these children are diagnosed and subsequently enrolled in the programme.

a180.speaker: Petrus, clinic nurse
a180.name: Petrus
a180.title: clinic nurse
a180.speech: "We are grateful for this initiative by the U.S. government. We have been eagerly awaiting the delivery of RUTF to our clinics, as we have witnessed many children suffering from malnutrition. It has been years since we last received any supplies."

a180.speaker: April/September 2024 Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) analysis
a180.name: April/September 2024 Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) analysis
a180.speech: According to the IPC analysis, an estimated 1.4 million Namibians, nearly half of the country's population, are experiencing acute food insecurity - a figure that has doubled over the past 12 months.

a291.speaker: Chisi Mbewe, Red Arrows coach
a291.name: Chisi Mbewe
a291.title: Red Arrows coach
a291.speech: Warned against underrating Kabwe Warriors as the two giants prepare to face off in Sunday's ABSA Cup final at Heroes Stadium in Lusaka ; said Warriors will have to be treated with caution because they are not pushovers and their only hope of winning a trophy depends on scooping the ABSA Cup.

a291.speaker: Chisi Mbewe, Red Arrows coach
a291.name: Chisi Mbewe
a291.title: Red Arrows coach
a291.speech: Says Heroes is a perfect venue for the ABSA Cup final as it presents the Airmen a perfect opportunity to clinch a double ; said the playing tough at Heroes Stadium is similar to Nkoloma Stadium where the Airmen have not tasted defeat in the last nine home matches.

a337.speaker: Mr. Mahmud Hamid, administrator of the Rehei administrative area
a337.name: Mr. Mahmud Hamid
a337.title: administrator of the Rehei administrative area
a337.speech: Noted that water supply had been a major challenge for residents and expressed optimism that the micro-dam would significantly improve access to water for both humans and livestock.

a337.speaker: Mr. Girmatsion Abraha, administrator of the Halhal sub-zone, and Lt. Col. Gebreab Tsehaye, Commander of the 34th Division
a337.name: Mr. Girmatsion Abraha
a337.title: administrator of the Halhal sub-zone, and Lt. Col. Gebreab Tsehaye, Commander of the 34th Division
a337.speech: Emphasized that the collaborative effort between the public and Defense Forces was part of a broader integrated development program.

a337.speaker: Mr. Gebremeskel Tewolde, representative of the Ministry of Agriculture
a337.name: Mr. Gebremeskel Tewolde
a337.title: representative of the Ministry of Agriculture
a337.speech: Explained that in addition to providing potable water, the micro-dam would support the development of irrigation farming in the area.

a337.speaker: Ambassador Abdella Musa, Governor of the Anseba region
a337.name: Ambassador Abdella Musa
a337.title: Governor of the Anseba region
a337.speech: Praised the active involvement of Defense Forces members in various development initiatives aimed at improving public livelihoods.

a446.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin, chaired by President Patrice Talon (official communique)
a446.name: Council of Ministers of Benin
a446.title: chaired by President Patrice Talon (official communique)
a446.speech: Decided to transmit to the National Assembly, for examination and vote, the framework bill on construction and housing, stating that the initiative falls within the logic of improving construction and housing practices in the country, notably to correct the shortcomings observed over time, and that its adoption "will open a new era in the field of real-estate investment in Benin" ; the ministers concerned are instructed to support its discussion before the national representation.

a446.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin, chaired by President Patrice Talon (official communique)
a446.name: Council of Ministers of Benin
a446.title: chaired by President Patrice Talon (official communique)
a446.speech: Gave its agreement for the deployment of 2,431 Aspiring Teachers at the Ministry of Nursery and Primary Education for the 2024-2025 school year, from among the 2,513 candidates who passed the October 2022 test, in order to allow pupils of public primary schools to have one teacher per class.

a446.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin, chaired by President Patrice Talon (official communique)
a446.name: Council of Ministers of Benin
a446.title: chaired by President Patrice Talon (official communique)
a446.speech: Gave its agreement for contracting with various firms for the renovation of the former Marriott hotel in Cotonou, a 5-star complex, stating that to durably structure the tourism development dynamic under way it is important to consolidate the supply of hotel facilities and high-standard meeting infrastructure.

a446.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin, chaired by President Patrice Talon (official communique)
a446.name: Council of Ministers of Benin
a446.title: chaired by President Patrice Talon (official communique)
a446.speech: Authorised contracting for the study on the definitive repair of the sand-retention groyne built under the Millennium Challenge Account and handed to the Autonomous Port of Cotonou in 2011, in order to correct the persisting failings, with the ministers concerned to ensure the proper execution of the works.

a446.speaker: Independent international expert (consulted on the Cotonou sand-retention groyne)
a446.name: Independent international expert (consulted on the Cotonou sand-retention groyne)
a446.speech: Identified, as the primary cause of the deterioration of the groyne, negligence in the design of the infrastructure.

a446.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin, chaired by President Patrice Talon (official communique)
a446.name: Council of Ministers of Benin
a446.title: chaired by President Patrice Talon (official communique)
a446.speech: Authorised Benin's participation in the Agricultural Production Show in Rennes, France (17-19 September 2024), in the 69th session of the International Whaling Commission in Lima, Peru (22-27 September 2024), and the organisation in Cotonou of the second edition of the International Forum on the Living Environment (4-7 October 2024), and pronounced appointments at the Ministry of Energy, Water and Mines on the proposal of the minister.

a454.speaker: Abdullah Hammad, brother of the deceased Palestinian worker Raafat Abdul Aziz Abdullah Hammad
a454.name: Abdullah Hammad
a454.title: brother of the deceased Palestinian worker Raafat Abdul Aziz Abdullah Hammad
a454.speech: Said the family had refused the occupation authorities’ demand to carry out an autopsy on the body, and pointed out that the occupation is still withholding his body under the pretext of an “identity verification” ; added that the martyr’s body would be buried in his home town of Silwad, east of Ramallah, as soon as it arrived, and pointed out that the martyr was the father of three children (the eldest six years old, the youngest one year old).

a454.speaker: Jerusalem Governorate (official statement)
a454.name: Jerusalem Governorate (official statement)
a454.speech: Stated that this crime stands “in the context of a systematic policy of the occupation forces against Palestinian workers, who are forced to take on the risk of jumping over the apartheid wall, while the forces continue to shoot directly at them or fire tear gas and stun grenades at them, which in recent months has led to the martyrdom and injury of dozens of people.”

a533.speaker: United Nations (recommendation)
a533.name: United Nations (recommendation)
a533.speech: Previously, the United Nations recommendation was for at least 9 kilos of cereals per month (compared with the reduced World Food Programme ration of 3 kilos of rice, 1 kilo of peas and half a litre of cooking oil per person).

a594.speaker: Commentators
a594.name: Commentators
a594.speech: Said this week that while HIV/Aids remains a major public health issue, Namibia appears to be stemming the tide of the epidemic.

a594.speaker: UNAIDS
a594.name: UNAIDS
a594.speech: Has admitted that some groupings are not benefiting from Namibia's success in making sure a large population is aware of their HIV status.

a594.speaker: Puleng Letsie, UNAIDS fast-track advisor
a594.name: Puleng Letsie
a594.title: UNAIDS fast-track advisor
a594.speech: Said during a talk show on NBC television this week that although the country has done extremely well in achieving the United Nations targets, certain clusters of the population are left behind: "Even though the country was one of the first to achieve the target before the 2020 deadline, the success is not uniform across the population groups. Some population groups do not benefit from the success. These are usually young people, children and key populations" ; "That success is for the overall population but these groups are very low in terms of knowing their status and being on treatment. Young people and children on treatment are around 60%. We must weigh so that all the key populations can join the success" ; According to her, key populations include people who are vulnerable to HIV because of certain circumstances, people who are at high risk of acquiring HIV including the LGBTQI+ community, those who are in the lower quintals and economically disadvantaged and those who do sex work.

a594.speaker: Puleng Letsie, UNAIDS fast-track advisor
a594.name: Puleng Letsie
a594.title: UNAIDS fast-track advisor
a594.speech: Said Covid-19 has changed the dynamics such that resources, including human resources, were shifted: "HIV and other health issues and services were sort of disrupted. Linking this to almost 40 years of dealing with HIV, we have learnt great lessons. The great lessons learnt from HIV are now being used for Covid-19," citing community-based services, strategic information, surveillance, documentation and contact tracing as some examples.

a594.speaker: Namibian Ministry of Health (information)
a594.name: Namibian Ministry of Health (information)
a594.speech: According to information by the health ministry, 90% of Namibians do know their HIV status, 98% are on treatment and 91% have durable viral load suppression.

a594.speaker: Jess Long, US embassy chargé d'affaires
a594.name: Jess Long
a594.title: US embassy chargé d'affaires
a594.speech: Said Namibia is a global leader in constantly pushing forward to reach new audiences and making sure strong health systems exist not only for HIV but other pandemics ; "We have spent more than US$1.6 billion with Pepfar programme in Namibia since 2005 and this is money taken from the US taxpayers and the purpose of that is to save lives and advance global health security. If we aren't doing effective programmes, we are wasting money and risking people's lives."

a594.speaker: Jess Long, US embassy chargé d'affaires
a594.name: Jess Long
a594.title: US embassy chargé d'affaires
a594.speech: Has also praised the concerted efforts of the ministry of health, community members and the Pepfar programme in ensuring a large population has access to treatment: "There was a lot of thought put into this, increasing concrete-like access to medication and multi dispensing, so somebody has to only come once and get six months of medication instead of coming every month. There have been instances where one person in a community group gets medicine for many people at one time and the next time somebody else gets it."

a594.speaker: Jacque Kamangu, health ministry official
a594.name: Jacque Kamangu
a594.title: health ministry official
a594.speech: Admitted the Covid-19 pandemic disrupted HIV-related programmes.

a665.speaker: UNHCR, 2023 report
a665.name: UNHCR
a665.title: 2023 report
a665.speech: Described eastern Congo as one of the most dangerous places on earth, where women and children endure systemic violence.

a665.speaker: Government of Rwanda
a665.name: Government of Rwanda
a665.speech: Suspended its 2024-2029 development cooperation with Belgium, condemning the European country for interfering with regional peace efforts and politicizing development finance.

a665.speaker: Dambisa Moyo, economist, in her book 'Dead Aid'
a665.name: Dambisa Moyo
a665.title: economist, in her book 'Dead Aid'
a665.speech: Argued that Africa has received over a trillion dollars in aid since the 1960s and that, rather than catalyzing prosperity, this influx of foreign funds has entrenched dependency, weakened governance, and perpetuated economic stagnation.

a697.speaker: Felix Kwakye Ofosu, Minister of State responsible for Government Communications
a697.name: Felix Kwakye Ofosu
a697.title: Minister of State responsible for Government Communications
a697.speech: Says the government has saved over GH₵400 million by restructuring the Office of the President, as part of efforts to reduce public spending; speaking in a radio interview with GBC on Thursday [May 8, 2025], said the restructuring forms part of measures taken during President John Dramani Mahama's first 120 days in office ; "If you look at the budget, you see that there have been cuts in goods and services, and capital expenditure. In the Office of the President alone, over GH₵400 million has been saved," he said ; attributed these reductions to the President's decision to form a "lean" government, saying the number of ministers and deputies has been reduced from 126 under the previous administration to 56.

a697.speaker: Felix Kwakye Ofosu, Minister of State responsible for Government Communications
a697.name: Felix Kwakye Ofosu
a697.title: Minister of State responsible for Government Communications
a697.speech: Said his own ministry illustrates the reduced scale of government operations: "I am Minister for Government Communications; I also double as the President's spokesperson. Just before we came to power, the President's communication outfit alone had 28 people," he explained ; said the current setup has only seven staff members handling the same tasks: "All that is done now by seven people," he added, arguing that the government is demonstrating how to manage with fewer resources.

a697.speaker: Felix Kwakye Ofosu, Minister of State responsible for Government Communications
a697.name: Felix Kwakye Ofosu
a697.title: Minister of State responsible for Government Communications
a697.speech: Responding to claims that the government was making up for the reduced number of ministers by increasing appointments to state agencies, dismissed the suggestion as "simply untrue", saying cuts had been applied across the government.

a697.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a697.name: John Dramani Mahama
a697.title: President of Ghana
a697.speech: Gave an account of his first 120 days in office in a televised address.

a698.speaker: Dr. Cecilia Kanyama, University of North Carolina (UNC) Project in Malawi
a698.name: Dr. Cecilia Kanyama
a698.title: University of North Carolina (UNC) Project in Malawi
a698.speech: In an interview with Maravi Post on Wednesday, April 22, said AIDS-related illnesses killed 390,000 people in Africa in 2023; said 130,000 of those deaths were from cryptococcal meningitis, a deadly brain infection and the second leading cause of HIV-related deaths ; said the Drugs for Neglected Diseases Initiative (DNDi) and partners have started testing a new treatment for cryptococcal meningitis in Malawi and Tanzania ; "The new treatment could save lives and help health workers in poor areas facing funding cuts by making care simpler and more effective."

a728.speaker: Blessings Chiwosi, Malawian youth ambassador and student at China Agricultural University
a728.name: Blessings Chiwosi
a728.title: Malawian youth ambassador and student at China Agricultural University
a728.speech: “I feel it is every citizen’s duty to utilize such opportunities for the betterment of our country’s development,” he said, adding that “Malawi has a lot of resources that can attract noble investors for her economic growth, hence taking part in this cultural event.” ; “I am representing Malawi not only because it is less popular in other parts of the world but also for positioning it for socioeconomic returns to address challenges that people face, which need innovative ways and solutions through tourism.”

a1030.speaker: Ethiopian Airlines and the United States
a1030.name: Ethiopian Airlines and the United States
a1030.speech: announced a new partnership agreement that will enable the nation's flagship carrier Ethiopian Airlines to source locally grown produce and ingredients for preparing in-flight meals for global passengers.

a1030.speaker: Tewolde GebreMariam, Ethiopian Airlines Group CEO
a1030.name: Tewolde GebreMariam
a1030.title: Ethiopian Airlines Group CEO
a1030.speech: “We deeply value our relationship with USAID and extend our appreciation to USAID for all the support. The new partnership consolidates our effort to continue providing high-quality inflight meals to global passengers while intensifying our effort in creating an enabling environment for local farmers across the value chain. We would like to maintain our partnership with USAID on a range of spheres.”

a1030.speaker: Michael Raynor, U.S. Ambassador to Ethiopia
a1030.name: Michael Raynor
a1030.title: U.S. Ambassador to Ethiopia
a1030.speech: “The partnership we're launching today demonstrates what's achievable when prominent businesses like Ethiopian Airlines invest in other Ethiopian businesses and individuals, resulting in truly home-grown economic success that has the potential to be a model for other sectors.”

a1235.speaker: His Excellency Shimizu Fumio, Ambassador of Japan to Eswatini
a1235.name: His Excellency Shimizu Fumio
a1235.title: Ambassador of Japan to Eswatini
a1235.speech: in his speech expressed his enthusiasm for participating in this pivotal event, underscoring Japan’s long-standing commitment to supporting the people of Eswatini, and stated: “This support aligns with Japan’s mission to eradicate hunger and malnutrition, enabling vulnerable children to pursue their dreams.”

a1235.speaker: Dr. Tambo Gina, Minister of Economic Planning and Development of Eswatini
a1235.name: Dr. Tambo Gina
a1235.title: Minister of Economic Planning and Development of Eswatini
a1235.speech: expressed heartfelt gratitude for Japan’s unwavering support and highlighted how this initiative aligns with Eswatini’s National Development Plan (NDP) 2023/24 – 2027/28, emphasising the shared vision of reducing poverty and improving the quality of life for all citizens.

a1235.speaker: Ministry of Economic Planning and Development of Eswatini
a1235.name: Ministry of Economic Planning and Development of Eswatini
a1235.speech: extended heartfelt thanks to the Government of Japan for its generous support, which is expected to have a lasting impact on the lives of thousands of children in Eswatini.

a1372.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
a1372.name: Nangolo Mbumba
a1372.title: President of Namibia
a1372.speech: "has appealed to the United Nations General Assembly to support the modalities to actualize the advisory opinion rendered by the International Court of Justice regarding the ongoing conflict in Gaza": "Prolonged occupation does not justify or make acceptable the hardships and injustices endured. This is particularly true for the people of Gaza, who continue to be brutally massacred. As a country that has endured genocide, Namibia believes that Israel, by intent and by action, is committing genocide. Namibia continues to call for a ceasefire and for humanitarian assistance to flow unhindered into Gaza."

a1372.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
a1372.name: Nangolo Mbumba
a1372.title: President of Namibia
a1372.speech: Repeated Namibia's call for the lifting of decades-old US blockades against Cuba and Zimbabwe: "Economic hardships continue to affect the sister Republic of Cuba, in stark contrast to the ideals of inclusivity and the goal of leaving no one behind. Namibia calls for the end of the economic, financial, and commercial blockade against Cuba. Namibia also reiterates its call for the immediate and unconditional lifting of illegal sanctions against Zimbabwe, which hinders the country's capacity to achieve Sustainable Development Goals."

a1372.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
a1372.name: Nangolo Mbumba
a1372.title: President of Namibia
a1372.speech: Said the quest for self-determination for the Sahrawi people remains a matter the world body should help intensify, and reminded the Assembly that continued disenfranchisement of the people of Western Sahara is an affront to the UN Charter, its purposes and principles, and that this year's session must change this.

a1372.speaker: International Court of Justice (advisory opinion)
a1372.name: International Court of Justice (advisory opinion)
a1372.speech: "stated that Israel's continued occupation of the Gaza Strip and West Bank is a violation of international law" and "further outlined that Israel end the war".

a1373.speaker: Jeremiah Mwaungulu, director of Rev Bolamoyo
a1373.name: Jeremiah Mwaungulu
a1373.title: director of Rev Bolamoyo
a1373.speech: "This drama may have multiple meanings, but we are not drawing a conclusion. Instead, we want to allow the audience to reflect on the message and make their own interpretations" ; commenting on the slanting of the production, said a lot is happening in the country and they look at the play as a platform to share critical message about the country's political developments: "As artists, we are duty-bound to provide a commentary. Art is activism and we cannot keep quite amid so many things happening."

a1373.speaker: Jeremiah Mwaungulu, director of Rev Bolamoyo
a1373.name: Jeremiah Mwaungulu
a1373.title: director of Rev Bolamoyo
a1373.speech: Played down any inferences of the play's title to Bagamoyo: "That is the interpretation we have seen on the social media, but the title has nothing to do with Bagamoyo as is suggested. This is just the name of one of the characters in the play. I know people will draw a lot of parallels that we cannot control."

a1373.speaker: Anthony Masamba, production manager
a1373.name: Anthony Masamba
a1373.title: production manager
a1373.speech: Said their silence since their debut production should not be construed as inactivity; said theatre requires one to have a good reason to come up with a production, time to prepare and resources to support the production: "For us, this is political activism, giving a voice to others. We may have the message, but packaging it takes time. Lack of resources is also a hindrance. From experience, stage play production without sponsorship can really be a nightmare."

a1373.speaker: Catholic bishops of Malawi (pastoral letter)
a1373.name: Catholic bishops of Malawi (pastoral letter)
a1373.speech: In their pastoral letter earlier this year, "said Malawi had missed the route to 'the promised land' of Canaan and was stuck in this town [Bagamoyo]."

a1696.speaker: Joseph Dion Ngute (Joseph Deol Ngoti), Prime Minister of Cameroon
a1696.name: Joseph Dion Ngute (Joseph Deol Ngoti)
a1696.title: Prime Minister of Cameroon
a1696.speech: Affirmed his country's support for the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation.

a1696.speaker: Joseph Dion Ngute (Joseph Deol Ngoti), Prime Minister of Cameroon
a1696.name: Joseph Dion Ngute (Joseph Deol Ngoti)
a1696.title: Prime Minister of Cameroon
a1696.speech: Stressed the centrality of the Palestinian question, the need to implement the two-State solution and to stop the aggression of the Israeli occupation against the Palestinian people.

a1696.speaker: Lejeune Mbella Mbella (Lugen Mbila Mbila), Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Cameroon
a1696.name: Lejeune Mbella Mbella (Lugen Mbila Mbila)
a1696.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Cameroon
a1696.speech: Delivered his country's address after assuming the presidency of the session, welcoming the guests of the fiftieth session, whose date coincides with the fiftieth anniversary of Cameroon's accession to the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation in 1974, and expressing his thanks to the President of the 49th session and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Mauritania, His Excellency Mr Mohamed Salem Ould Marzouk, for his good management of the previous session.

a1696.speaker: Lejeune Mbella Mbella (Lugen Mbila Mbila), Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Cameroon
a1696.name: Lejeune Mbella Mbella (Lugen Mbila Mbila)
a1696.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Cameroon
a1696.speech: Stressed the importance of the slogan of the fiftieth session, "Developing transport and communication infrastructure within the framework of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation: a key tool in the fight against poverty and insecurity", and underlined the importance of development and of establishing peace and security for member states, highlighting the escalation and violence in Palestine and affirming the principle of the two-State solution.

a1696.speaker: Hussein Ibrahim Taha, Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
a1696.name: Hussein Ibrahim Taha
a1696.title: Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
a1696.speech: Expressed his sincere thanks to the Cameroonian authorities for the measures and arrangements they made to ensure the success of the session, praising the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for its generous support to the organisation, under the generous patronage of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Crown Prince and Prime Minister.

a1696.speaker: Hussein Ibrahim Taha, Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
a1696.name: Hussein Ibrahim Taha
a1696.title: Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
a1696.speech: Explained that the cause of Palestine and Al-Quds Al-Sharif is witnessing serious developments that pose a challenge to the international community in general and to the OIC in particular, as the Israeli occupation forces continue their unprecedented military aggression against the Gaza Strip and all parts of the Palestinian territory, including the city of Al-Quds Al-Sharif, which has caused thousands of victims ; revealed that the organisation continues to make efforts to address the repercussions of the brutal Israeli aggression against the Palestinian people, to reinforce that people's steadfastness on its land and to defend its legitimate rights, stressing the need to join joint efforts to implement the resolutions of the UN Security Council and the UN General Assembly calling for an immediate and complete ceasefire and ensuring access to humanitarian aid to all parts of the Gaza Strip in an adequate and sustainable manner.

a1696.speaker: Hussein Ibrahim Taha, Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
a1696.name: Hussein Ibrahim Taha
a1696.title: Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
a1696.speech: Addressed the organisation's efforts in Afghanistan in the humanitarian field and within the framework of a constructive dialogue on various issues, in particular the continued ban on girls' education, women's work and their participation in public life, stressing that the organisation's efforts have continued through the ongoing visits of the Secretary General's special envoy, delegations of academics and the organisation's institutions concerned with Afghanistan, with the aim of engaging in dialogue with the de facto government to end this ban.

a1696.speaker: Hussein Ibrahim Taha, Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
a1696.name: Hussein Ibrahim Taha
a1696.title: Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
a1696.speech: Reiterated the OIC's principled position in support of the territorial integrity of the Republic of Azerbaijan, welcoming the end of the armed conflict between the Republic of Azerbaijan and the Republic of Armenia and the restoration of Azerbaijan's sovereignty and territorial integrity within its national borders, and expressing deep concern about the fate of the Azerbaijanis who had been forcibly expelled from the territory of present-day Armenia.

a1696.speaker: Hussein Ibrahim Taha, Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
a1696.name: Hussein Ibrahim Taha
a1696.title: Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
a1696.speech: Stressed that the organisation will continue its efforts to defend the interests of Muslim communities and societies in non-member countries, highlighting in this regard the question of the Rohingya Muslims in Myanmar and expressing his hope that this issue, which faces serious challenges, will receive more support and solidarity from member states ; stressed that the Organisation will pursue its efforts in the field of combating terrorism, countering manifestations of Islamophobia and religious hatred and promoting interreligious and intercultural dialogue in cooperation with international partners, noting that the Special Envoy of the OIC Secretary General for combating Islamophobia will soon take up his duties.

a1696.speaker: Hussein Ibrahim Taha, Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
a1696.name: Hussein Ibrahim Taha
a1696.title: Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
a1696.speech: Stressed that the organisation will pursue its efforts to prepare the donors' conference to support displaced persons and refugees in the Sahel region and the Lake Chad basin, scheduled for 26 October 2024 at the OIC headquarters in Jeddah, expressing his deep gratitude to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for kindly hosting this conference and for its commendable efforts to ensure the appropriate conditions for holding it.

a1696.speaker: Waleed bin Abdulkarim Al-Khereiji (Al-Khadi), Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1696.name: Waleed bin Abdulkarim Al-Khereiji (Al-Khadi)
a1696.title: Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1696.speech: Stressed in his address the importance of the role played by the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation since its creation in serving Islamic issues in various fields and in protecting the interests of Muslims by moving positively to face various challenges, expressing the Kingdom's aspirations to strengthen joint work on the issues of concern to the Islamic Ummah at various levels and to push joint Islamic action towards broader horizons and wider fields to ensure a better future for our Islamic nation.

a1696.speaker: Waleed bin Abdulkarim Al-Khereiji (Al-Khadi), Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1696.name: Waleed bin Abdulkarim Al-Khereiji (Al-Khadi)
a1696.title: Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1696.speech: Reiterated the Kingdom's condemnation and rejection of all forms of crimes against the Palestinian people by the Israeli occupation forces, saying: "The Israeli occupation forces are indifferent to international resolutions and laws, which have cost the lives of tens of thousands of Palestinians, most of them women, children and innocent civilians, amid the absence of international accountability and the inability of the Security Council to take deterrent measures." ; welcomed the Kingdom's declaration with brotherly countries to stop the Israeli aggression against the Palestinian people which, during its chairmanship of the ministerial committee emanating from the extraordinary Arab-Islamic summit in Riyadh, led a number of Western countries to recognise the brotherly State of Palestine, referring at the same time to the Arab-Islamic summit's decision on the creation of a legal centre to document violations.

a1696.speaker: Waleed bin Abdulkarim Al-Khereiji (Al-Khadi), Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1696.name: Waleed bin Abdulkarim Al-Khereiji (Al-Khadi)
a1696.title: Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1696.speech: Stressed that the Kingdom continues to provide relief assistance to civilians in the Gaza Strip with popular participation, through the popular campaign for the relief of the Palestinian people in the Gaza Strip launched by the King Salman Centre for Relief and Humanitarian Affairs, where the value of donations currently amounts to more than $185 million.

a1696.speaker: Waleed bin Abdulkarim Al-Khereiji (Al-Khadi), Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1696.name: Waleed bin Abdulkarim Al-Khereiji (Al-Khadi)
a1696.title: Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1696.speech: On the crisis in Sudan, reaffirmed the Kingdom's firm positions on maintaining Sudan's security and stability, and called in this regard for the parties to the Sudanese crisis to return to dialogue to spare brotherly Sudan.

a1696.speaker: Waleed bin Abdulkarim Al-Khereiji (Al-Khadi), Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1696.name: Waleed bin Abdulkarim Al-Khereiji (Al-Khadi)
a1696.title: Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1696.speech: On the Yemeni question, stressed the continuation of the government of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques in supporting efforts to resolve the crisis in brotherly Yemen and its quest for the return of peace, security and stability there, reaffirming the Kingdom's initiative to end the war and reach a comprehensive political solution, and warning against the danger of escalation in the Red Sea region, which undermines efforts to maintain the security and stability of international shipping corridors and global trade and threatens freedom of navigation and the growth of the world economy.

a1696.speaker: Waleed bin Abdulkarim Al-Khereiji (Al-Khadi), Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1696.name: Waleed bin Abdulkarim Al-Khereiji (Al-Khadi)
a1696.title: Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1696.speech: Stressed that the Kingdom has never hesitated to use all its potential in order to serve humanitarian causes and to work to provide development support to brotherly and friendly countries, for the growth and prosperity of the region and the world, welcoming member states, their institutions and international donor partners to the OIC donors' conference to be organised by the Kingdom in October 2024 ; revealed that the Kingdom is continuing its efforts alongside the Republic of the Maldives to organise a joint conference entitled "Strengthening integrity in the tourism sector" in order to promote the objectives of joint Islamic action, calling on the bodies concerned with combating corruption and with tourism in OIC member states to take part in this important conference.

a1696.speaker: Riad Mansour, head of the Palestinian delegation
a1696.name: Riad Mansour
a1696.title: head of the Palestinian delegation
a1696.speech: Gave a comprehensive briefing on the latest situation in Palestine, noting the president's initiative to travel to the Gaza Strip, referring to the advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice, and to the continuation of the campaign for recognition of the State of Palestine and for it to enjoy full membership of the United Nations.

a1704.speaker: Stake of the Nation forum, organised by MSDG (eighth edition)
a1704.name: Stake of the Nation forum
a1704.title: organised by MSDG (eighth edition)
a1704.speech: Reported that remittances from the Gambian diaspora have exceeded $775.6 million in 2024.

a1704.speaker: Official from the Central Bank of the Gambia (anonymous)
a1704.name: Official from the Central Bank of the Gambia (anonymous)
a1704.speech: According to an official from the Central Bank of the Gambia, this represents a notable increase of $28.8 million compared to the previous year.

a1704.speaker: Muhammed B.S. Jallow, Vice President of the Gambia
a1704.name: Muhammed B.S. Jallow
a1704.title: Vice President of the Gambia
a1704.speech: Said that on September 23, 2017, President Barrow announced the Gambia's first-ever diaspora policy at a town hall meeting in New York and declared December 15 to January 14 the Gambia Diaspora Month: "In the past eight years, this period witnessed a joyous celebration of homecoming, a full calendar of diaspora engagements, and a noticeable boost in diaspora tourism and the many benefits it brings to the local economy and the cultural industries," he stated.

a1704.speaker: Muhammed B.S. Jallow, Vice President of the Gambia
a1704.name: Muhammed B.S. Jallow
a1704.title: Vice President of the Gambia
a1704.speech: Said that in May 2024 the World Economic Forum (WEF) published an article recognizing The Gambia's leadership in this field, and invited development partners to support the Fourth Phase of the MSDG Project, which will run for five years from July 2024 to June 2029.

a1704.speaker: Muhammed B.S. Jallow, Vice President of the Gambia
a1704.name: Muhammed B.S. Jallow
a1704.title: Vice President of the Gambia
a1704.speech: Disclosed that: "2025 is the year that the United Nations convenes the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development (FFD4), to be held in Seville, Spain between June 30 and July 3, 2025. The outcome document will replace the 2015 Addis Ababa Action Agenda as the global framework on development finance. The role of diaspora and innovative finance must be prominent in the consultations, proceedings, content, recommendations, and commitments of FFD4."

a1704.speaker: Muhammed B.S. Jallow, Vice President of the Gambia
a1704.name: Muhammed B.S. Jallow
a1704.title: Vice President of the Gambia
a1704.speech: "The Gambia has dedicated the Eighth Stake in the Nation Forum (SNF8) to the theme 'Diaspora, Jobs and the Financing for Development' theme. In line with our Diaspora Policy and the strategy and work plans of the Gambia Diaspora and Migration Directorate (GDMD), the government will continue to champion innovations in diaspora investment and development. In 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, MSDG piloted a Diaspora Development Fund (DDF)," he stated ; revealed that in the last audited results in June 2024, half a million Euros in cash, equivalent to 37 million dalasi, were awarded as grants to 74 projects: "Professionals led these projects from the diaspora who worked with local partners in rural and urban Gambia. The projects, in turn, generated four million Euros, equivalent to 295 million dalasi, through cash and in-kind co-finance from the diaspora, government, and other partners."

a1704.speaker: Muhammed B.S. Jallow, Vice President of the Gambia
a1704.name: Muhammed B.S. Jallow
a1704.title: Vice President of the Gambia
a1704.speech: "It is a solemn commitment to make the diaspora an integral part of our national development strategy. It acknowledges the diaspora as not only contributors of remittances but also as a source of invaluable expertise, innovation, and global networks that can serve as catalysts for transformative care, and I always say that even beyond the Gambia, the mud, talked about African Renaissance cannot happen without the diaspora," said Vice president Jallow ; added that the forum also intends to outline the implementation of diaspora and innovative finance initiatives, ethical migrant labor programs, action points on diaspora jobs, and development financing.

a1704.speaker: Mamadou Tangara, Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, and Gambians Abroad
a1704.name: Mamadou Tangara
a1704.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, and Gambians Abroad
a1704.speech: In delivering his statement, said the initiative symbolizes the enduring bond between the diaspora and the homeland and also reaffirms the recognition of the diaspora as the eighth region of the Gambia, a historic declaration made by President Barrow in 2018 and enshrined in the fourth pillar of the recovery focus, the national development plan, NDP, 2023 to 2027.

a1704.speaker: Chukwu-Emeka Chikezie, MBE, Pioneer of Global Diaspora Development and Practice, Co-Founder of AFFORD (UK) and Country Director of the International Growth Centre (IGC) Sierra Leone
a1704.name: Chukwu-Emeka Chikezie
a1704.title: MBE, Pioneer of Global Diaspora Development and Practice, Co-Founder of AFFORD (UK) and Country Director of the International Growth Centre (IGC) Sierra Leone
a1704.speech: Congratulated the Government of the Gambia; according to him, it is worth noting that what you are doing in the Gambia is not necessarily practiced in other African countries.

a1704.speaker: Chukwu-Emeka Chikezie, MBE, Pioneer of Global Diaspora Development and Practice, Co-Founder of AFFORD (UK) and Country Director of the International Growth Centre (IGC) Sierra Leone
a1704.name: Chukwu-Emeka Chikezie
a1704.title: MBE, Pioneer of Global Diaspora Development and Practice, Co-Founder of AFFORD (UK) and Country Director of the International Growth Centre (IGC) Sierra Leone
a1704.speech: Said that overseas development assistance is declining: "Today, the major donor countries spend about 14-13% of their overseas development corporations in their countries dealing with crises like the refugee crisis in Ukraine. So, we must recognize that, as Africans, we must take responsibility for our development." ; "One of the tasks, and I would like to put this on the floor of Professor Faal and his team, is for us to begin to measure the other contributions to have a more realistic and holistic measure of this contribution. When we do that, we will find that we are already our own greatest aid donors," he stated ; also disclosed that the dialogue between the diaspora, the government, and the other stakeholders is critical.

a1776.speaker: Igor Burkin, Chargé d'Affaires a.i. of the Russian Federation in Burkina Faso
a1776.name: Igor Burkin
a1776.title: Chargé d'Affaires a.i. of the Russian Federation in Burkina Faso
a1776.speech: "This donation was motivated first of all by the situation currently prevailing in Africa, and more particularly in the Sahel. There are currently displaced people as a result of terrorist actions, and it is precisely these displaced populations who are destitute and in need. Russia is here to help African countries, and Burkina Faso in particular." ; He recalled that since 2003 his country has paid out more than 430 million dollars to support WFP humanitarian operations around the world, placing it among the UN agency's 20 main donors. ; He said that hunger and food shortages in Africa, particularly in the Sahel region, are exacerbated by the security crisis, and that the humanitarian aid, sent by the Russian Ministry of Civil Defence and Emergency Situations, had successfully reached Burkina Faso: "This gesture underlines the traditionally friendly character of relations between the Russian Federation and Burkina Faso."

a1776.speaker: Sory Ouane, WFP Representative and Country Director in Burkina Faso
a1776.name: Sory Ouane
a1776.title: WFP Representative and Country Director in Burkina Faso
a1776.speech: Expressed his gratitude to the donor: "This donation testifies to your strong commitment to supporting humanitarian efforts in a particularly difficult context." ; He highlighted the role of WFP's logistics and recalled that the Burkinabè government has made food security a priority, and that WFP, aligned with the Sustainable Development Goal, must support Burkina Faso in its efforts to eradicate hunger and improve nutrition.

a2004.speaker: Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) (public notice)
a2004.name: Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) (public notice)
a2004.speech: Required owners of electric motor vehicles such as motorcycles and tricycles to register and fix number plates from 16 May to 30 June 2025, noting an increase in the use of these vehicles, especially in urban areas, often without registration or official identification, which contributes to an increase in crime and in accidents with no legal follow-up: “The TRA wishes to inform the public that, from 16 May to 30 June 2025, all users of such vehicles, including motorcycles, tricycles and others, are required to register and fix these plates within the time given” ; “This requirement is in accordance with the Road Traffic Act, 1973, Section 8 (1), which requires every user of a motor vehicle on the road to fulfil that obligation. After that date, legal measures will be taken against all those who do not carry out that duty” ; reminded the public that it has improved the motor vehicle registration system, available through the TRA website (www.tra.go.tz) or at TRA offices throughout the country.

a2004.speaker: Ally Mahamudu, resident of Mbezi (motorcycle user)
a2004.name: Ally Mahamudu
a2004.title: resident of Mbezi (motorcycle user)
a2004.speech: Said he does not know whether there is a notice requiring them to fit registration numbers on small rechargeable motorcycles, and that even if they have decided so, it is not bad because there is nothing to be done if the government has spoken: “We are not opposing registration, but the Government should create a friendly environment. Most of these motorcycles we use just to make ends meet; even the profit itself is small, because these motorcycles are not for business.”

a2004.speaker: Sada Musa, tricycle (guta) driver at Mbezi Sokoni
a2004.name: Sada Musa
a2004.title: tricycle (guta) driver at Mbezi Sokoni
a2004.speech: Said tricycle drivers in the Mbezi area have no information requiring them to register because their market leadership is asleep: “Until today I do not know where we start registering, because our market leadership has not given us any information so far. Even the TRA have not reached us directly to provide education. If they show us the way, we are ready.”

a2004.speaker: Joel Mwampamba, boda boda driver in Temeke
a2004.name: Joel Mwampamba
a2004.title: boda boda driver in Temeke
a2004.speech: Supported the TRA decision: “We are tired of seeing unidentified motorcycles involved in crime and then the driver disappears without being known. Registration numbers will help a great deal with that.”

a2007.speaker: Ben Nangombe, Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a2007.name: Ben Nangombe
a2007.title: Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a2007.speech: Reiterated that Namibia has made commendable progress in curbing the spread of infectious diseases like HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria ; "We have witnessed significant forward movement in achieving the goals articulated in the National Strategic Framework, thanks in large part to the invaluable support by our Development Cooperation Partners and the active role of Civil Society Organisations (CSOs). The data and figures towards Namibia's achievements of the UNAIDS 95-95-95 fast-tracked targets for HIV are well known to all of you. As of 2022 in Namibia, 94% of HIV-positive individuals know their status, 97% of them are on antiretroviral therapy (ART), and 93% have reached viral suppression (94-97-93)." ; "This is the last mile, and we dare not relent. We will not falter. Not now, when we have achieved so much. Let us maintain the momentum and deliver a solid NOP and a comprehensive sustainability framework to operationalise our NSF for HIV, TB, malaria, and hepatitis."

a2007.speaker: Cheryl Amoroso, PEPFAR Representative
a2007.name: Cheryl Amoroso
a2007.title: PEPFAR Representative
a2007.speech: Discussed the funding perspective of PEPFAR as a donor: "From a PEPFAR perspective, we need to already embrace change to together understand the transformation of HIV programming in line with this developing vision that the country has for its future health system, not just from an HIV perspective but holistically. From a donor viewpoint, we are ready to adapt our investments to help realise this developing vision, which is why today and tomorrow are so important. We will use this roadmap to guide our investment. The Namibia PEPFAR investments have already started making shifts better aligned with the future vision that is already developing, and the clarity that we will have on this documentation will continue to support that transition."

a2008.speaker: OTRACO (Burundi public transport office)
a2008.name: OTRACO (Burundi public transport office)
a2008.speech: Has just thrown in the towel, admitting it is no longer able to take children to school because there is no fuel.

a2008.speaker: Ministry of Trade (Burundi)
a2008.name: Ministry of Trade (Burundi)
a2008.speech: Has given up, not daring to set prices for phantom vehicles.

a2008.speaker: SOSUMO (Moso Sugar Company)
a2008.name: SOSUMO (Moso Sugar Company)
a2008.speech: Declared more than a year ago that it was suspending its activities.

a2008.speaker: Foreign exchange market players
a2008.name: Foreign exchange market players
a2008.speech: Admit that the situation is not about to change, as the Burundian franc goes into free fall after an estimated 26% depreciation last year.

a2008.speaker: Experts and organisations that closely follow the Burundian economy
a2008.name: Experts and organisations that closely follow the Burundian economy
a2008.speech: Speak of self-strangulation policies, the inertia of the authorities in the face of the ills eating away at governance leading to a suffocation with no way out.

a2008.speaker: William Shakespeare (in Hamlet)
a2008.name: William Shakespeare (in Hamlet)
a2008.speech: “When sorrows come, they come not single spies but in battalions.”

a2008.speaker: Epidemiology experts
a2008.name: Epidemiology experts
a2008.speech: Say that cholera spreads at very high speed, which requires permanent emergency interventions.

a2008.speaker: The number one (President of Burundi)
a2008.name: The number one (President of Burundi)
a2008.speech: Keeps proclaiming loud and clear that Burundi is Eden, the proof being that it has tonnes of stockpiles of foodstuffs of every kind and that on top of that “it is rich.”

a2008.speaker: Head of government (Prime Minister of Burundi)
a2008.name: Head of government (Prime Minister of Burundi)
a2008.speech: Acknowledges that the country is going through a crisis of such gravity that he simultaneously admits his powerlessness to find solutions.

a2008.speaker: The ruling one-party-state system
a2008.name: The ruling one-party-state system
a2008.speech: Declares at every turn that it is not about to let go, going so far as to push aside, for the umpteenth time, the one and only person capable of challenging it: “It’s us or no one!”

a2087.speaker: foreignassistance.gov, official US data
a2087.name: foreignassistance.gov
a2087.title: official US data
a2087.speech: According to official data published by foreignassistance.gov, Eswatini's total US foreign assistance allocation dropped from USD 76.6 million (about E1.38 billion) in 2024 to USD 20.9 million (about E378 million) in 2025 - a 72.7% decrease ; according to foreignassistance.gov, between 2022 and 2024, the majority of US funding went toward HIV/AIDS, health systems, and related social support programmes.

a2087.speaker: Khanya Mabuza, Principal Secretary, Ministry of Health of Eswatini
a2087.name: Khanya Mabuza
a2087.title: Principal Secretary, Ministry of Health of Eswatini
a2087.speech: Assured that the country was planning to take over funded programmes by 2030 and outlined an operational plan agreement with the US detailing how Eswatini would sustain services if partner support ended: "Eswatini is among the African states planning to procure its own HIV treatment by 2030. Currently, partners are only providing line two and other drugs, while the government pays for line one, which is in high demand." ; "The roadmap states that in two years, the country will contribute 60%, with partners covering 40%. By 2030, the government would sustain HIV programmes on its own."

a2087.speaker: Khanya Mabuza, Principal Secretary, Ministry of Health of Eswatini
a2087.name: Khanya Mabuza
a2087.title: Principal Secretary, Ministry of Health of Eswatini
a2087.speech: Asked if the government was ready to sustain programmes like rural home visits, health services, and gender-based violence interventions, the PS said plans were being developed to incorporate them into government systems: "The country has integration plans for different programmes, as some will be fitted into the various ministries."

a2087.speaker: Ministry of Health of Eswatini, 2025/26 first quarter report
a2087.name: Ministry of Health of Eswatini
a2087.title: 2025/26 first quarter report
a2087.speech: The impact of the US Government's Stop Work Order, issued on January 25, 2025, was acknowledged; it has already significantly impacted HIV services, leading to a downturn in HIV testing from 27,334 individuals in April to 18,801 by June.

a2087.speaker: Local NGOs in Eswatini
a2087.name: Local NGOs in Eswatini
a2087.speech: Report fewer community health visits, and some outreach activities have been halted entirely; clinics supported by US partners report fewer resources to conduct testing and outreach.

a2163.speaker: Ronnie Varkevisser, CEO of the Namibian Manufacturers Association (NMA)
a2163.name: Ronnie Varkevisser
a2163.title: CEO of the Namibian Manufacturers Association (NMA)
a2163.speech: According to Varkevisser, manufacturing remains a catalyst for domestic economic growth despite Covid-19 taking a serious toll on the association and its membership base. During an exclusive interview with New Era, Varkevisser informed that the NMA lost various members since the advent of the pandemic, having a severe impact on their membership number. "Many of the bigger companies were able to diversify their production, with many producing masks and hand sanitizer, but the smaller players were left with no option but to either scale down or cease operations." ; Said the overall impact of this state of affairs is that Namibia's manufacturing base is "moving backwards" as some eight years ago the domestic manufacturing industry contributed an estimated 17% to the country's GDP compared to the current dismal 9%.

a2163.speaker: Ronnie Varkevisser, CEO of the Namibian Manufacturers Association (NMA)
a2163.name: Ronnie Varkevisser
a2163.title: CEO of the Namibian Manufacturers Association (NMA)
a2163.speech: Lamented: "Support for the sector should be focused for Namibia to become an industrialised nation. However, the alignment of different ministries to achieve this goal is lacking." He mentioned the Growth at Home strategy which he called "a brilliant document with sound policies", but questioned the implementation of the strategy, saying, "the execution is not taking place fast enough." ; Warned: "A case in point is the current situation of the Retail Charter and even the new Procurement Act. What is the current situation and what is the negative impact on local manufacturing growth because of slow execution? The manufacturing industry is suffering because of the slow implementation of these policies."

a2163.speaker: Ronnie Varkevisser, CEO of the Namibian Manufacturers Association (NMA)
a2163.name: Ronnie Varkevisser
a2163.title: CEO of the Namibian Manufacturers Association (NMA)
a2163.speech: Expressed concern about Namibia's ability to benefit from the Africa Free Trade Agreement, saying much collaboration still needs to take place before individual countries can reap the fruits of this ambitious continental endeavour: "Issues such as the Rules of Origin in the African Free Trade agreement are still a huge factor. Most of this red tape still needs to be eliminated before manufacturers in Namibia and on the continent can truly see the benefits from this agreement."

a2163.speaker: Ronnie Varkevisser, CEO of the Namibian Manufacturers Association (NMA)
a2163.name: Ronnie Varkevisser
a2163.title: CEO of the Namibian Manufacturers Association (NMA)
a2163.speech: "It is our constant input to all relevant industry topics that have earned NMA wide recognition not only from its members and other private sector organisations but also from our line Ministry which is the Ministry of Industrialisation and Trade."

a2163.speaker: Ronnie Varkevisser, CEO of the Namibian Manufacturers Association (NMA)
a2163.name: Ronnie Varkevisser
a2163.title: CEO of the Namibian Manufacturers Association (NMA)
a2163.speech: At the Namibia Exporter of the Year Awards event, Varkevisser reiterated the NMA's commitment to continuing the partnership with USAID in staging the annual awards going forward: "The exporter awards are an important milestone in recognising the valuable work that export firms play in Namibia, and we are glad to partner with the USAID TradeHub in this regard and look forward to our future collaboration to grow the awards."

a2174.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a2174.name: Joseph Boakai
a2174.title: President of Liberia
a2174.speech: has reassured the United States of Liberia's openness to strategic partnership in the areas of trade, energy, infrastructure, agriculture, technology, and entrepreneurship, among others; announced that his administration is building a foreign policy architecture that seeks not only to deepen political alliances but also to create strategic economic partnerships ; "The goal is to promote Liberia as a viable and attractive destination for investment, innovation, and sustainable development." ; his administration stands committed to creating a stable, transparent, and enabling environment for business ; recognized the critical role of the U.S. Private Sector and expressed optimism about the creation of pathways that foster increased engagement between Liberian and American businesses.

a2174.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a2174.name: Joseph Boakai
a2174.title: President of Liberia
a2174.speech: extolled the historical ties between Liberia and the U.S., while calling for a stronger economic partnership between both countries, and underscored the unique and enduring relationship between Liberia and the U.S., highlighting a shared history that spans over two centuries: "The U.S. has remained a steadfast ally, supporting Liberia in its democratic journey, providing development assistance, strengthening institutions, and most importantly, standing with Liberia during moments of national challenge."

a2174.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a2174.name: Joseph Boakai
a2174.title: President of Liberia
a2174.speech: described the celebration of the United States' 249th Independence Day as the birth of an enduring idea that freedom, democracy, and opportunity should be the bedrock upon which nations are built.

a2259.speaker: Debebe Eshetu, Ethiopian actor
a2259.name: Debebe Eshetu
a2259.title: Ethiopian actor
a2259.speech: "The police seemed very annoyed as he stopped us and was surely going to call the traffic police on us," says Debebe ; "'We've been rehearsing for tomorrow's live broadcast, and it's because you guys are here that we feel so safe,' recounts Debebe of what Woubshet said. "By the time Woubshet was finished chatting him up, the police officer was promising he would notify the traffic police so they would not give us trouble as we went on."

a2259.speaker: Woubshet Workalemahu, Ethiopian advertising pioneer, actor and poet (as recounted by Debebe Eshetu)
a2259.name: Woubshet Workalemahu
a2259.title: Ethiopian advertising pioneer, actor and poet (as recounted by Debebe Eshetu)
a2259.speech: Ran to the police with open arms, kissed him on both cheeks and said loudly, "Thank God you're here." ; He used to advise that everyone prepare what they planned to wear the night before, never in the morning: "He used to tell us that we were artists and should dress as such," says Debebe.

a2259.speaker: Dawit Yifru, renowned keyboardist and music arranger
a2259.name: Dawit Yifru
a2259.title: renowned keyboardist and music arranger
a2259.speech: "Dramatist, poet and actor, he was above all so easy to get along with," says Dawit of his friend. "He was anecdotal and knew a great deal of history." ; "The way he dressed, his height and facial structure reminded me a great deal of Haile Selassie," says Dawit.

a2259.speaker: Leul Getaneh, nephew of Woubshet Workalemahu
a2259.name: Leul Getaneh
a2259.title: nephew of Woubshet Workalemahu
a2259.speech: Said the cloak Woubshet wore was actually given to him by the Emperor, for a piece of poetry he penned, in a play he portrayed at Hager Fiker Theatre ; "He considered being well-dressed representative of his respect for others. Every day before he went to bed, he would carefully prepare what he would wear the next day. He would even iron out his socks." ; "He loved his work almost as much as he loved his children."

a2270.speaker: Republic of Djibouti (official statement)
a2270.name: Republic of Djibouti (official statement)
a2270.speech: Condemns in the strongest terms the decision of the Israeli occupation authorities to fully invade the Gaza Strip, considering this measure a grave escalation that adds to a series of crimes and flagrant violations committed against the brotherly Palestinian people, including policies of blockade, starvation, systematic destruction and forced displacement.

a2270.speaker: Republic of Djibouti (official statement)
a2270.name: Republic of Djibouti (official statement)
a2270.speech: Calls on the international community to assume its legal, moral and humanitarian responsibilities, and to act urgently and decisively to put an end to this escalation, prevent new crimes against the defenceless Palestinian people, guarantee the protection of civilians, and ensure the safe, sustained and unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip.

a2312.speaker: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a2312.name: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a2312.speech: has appealed to Sudan’s warring parties to uphold international humanitarian law and take concrete steps to protect civilians, as the country prepares to mark the anniversary of a devastating civil war.

a2312.speaker: Mirjana Spoljaric, ICRC President (press statement)
a2312.name: Mirjana Spoljaric
a2312.title: ICRC President (press statement)
a2312.speech: underscored the heavy toll the conflict has inflicted on millions of Sudanese civilians: "Two years of ruinous civil war have been seared into the lives of millions of Sudanese. The conflict has flared across the country, engulfing urban areas and urban centers. Civilians are trapped in a relentless nightmare of death and destruction," Spoljaric said ; "Civilians are killed and injured, their homes looted, and their livelihoods destroyed. Sexual violence is rampant and seeding trauma that will reverberate for generations."

a2312.speaker: Mirjana Spoljaric, ICRC President
a2312.name: Mirjana Spoljaric
a2312.title: ICRC President
a2312.speech: further noted that humanitarian workers and first responders are also deliberately attacked while carrying out their lifesaving work, and stated that the conflict is made deadlier by intentional attacks on civilian infrastructure ; warned that the horrors inflicted on civilians in Sudan should never be seen as inevitable consequences of war, adding a ceasefire would give people desperately needed respite; according to him, much of the suffering over the last two years would have been prevented had the rules of war been followed ; "Reductions in humanitarian funding are deepening this misery. As the conflict enters its third year, I call on the parties to the conflict to honor the commitments they made in Jeddah to uphold international humanitarian law and take concrete steps today to protect civilians. To do anything but only fuels more violence, more death, more destruction that Sudan—and the world—cannot afford."

a2312.speaker: Activists who spoke to French news agency AFP
a2312.name: Activists who spoke to French news agency AFP
a2312.speech: said the paramilitary RSF and its allies have recently killed 56 civilians over two days in attacks on a newly-retaken town in El-Fasher in North Darfur.

a2312.speaker: A network of volunteers coordinating aid across Sudan
a2312.name: A network of volunteers coordinating aid across Sudan
a2312.speech: said the killings, which occurred on April 11 and 12, targeted residents in Um Kadadah, around 180 kilometers east of El-Fasher.

a2312.speaker: United Nations
a2312.name: United Nations
a2312.speech: said more than 100 people were feared dead in RSF attacks on El-Fasher and two nearby famine-hit camps for displaced people.

a2312.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a2312.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a2312.speech: reiterated its call on the warring parties and their allies to ensure that civilians, humanitarian personnel, and medical teams are protected ; MSF said all restrictions on the movement of humanitarian supplies and staff must be removed, especially as the rainy season fast approaches.

a2312.speaker: Claire San Filippo, MSF Emergency Coordinator
a2312.name: Claire San Filippo
a2312.title: MSF Emergency Coordinator
a2312.speech: "The warring parties are not only failing to protect civilians. They are actively compounding their suffering," says Claire San Filippo ; "Wherever you look in Sudan, you will find needs overwhelming, urgent, and unmet. Millions are receiving almost no humanitarian assistance, medical facilities and staff remain under attack, and the global humanitarian system is failing to deliver even a fraction of what’s required."

a2312.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2312.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2312.speech: According to the WHO, more than 70 percent of health facilities in conflict-affected areas are barely operational or have closed, leaving millions of people without access to critical care.

a2346.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia
a2346.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a2346.title: President of Zambia
a2346.speech: Says suspension of United States Agency for International Development (USAID) programmes globally by the Trump administration is long overdue and a wake-up call for African countries to grow their economies by enhancing bilateral trade and investment among themselves ; says the development also calls for prudent management of resources and notes that socio-economic growth can only be attained with increased investment, trade and transaction among African countries ; welcomed United States President Donald Trump's order to freeze funding to all UNAIDS programmes ; "It is long overdue, it is actually long overdue because it underscores the importance of us on the continent growing our economies, focusing on growth, growth and more growth."

a2346.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2346.name: Donald Trump
a2346.title: US President
a2346.speech: Has called for the closure of USAID citing unprecedented levels of corruption.

a2346.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAIDS executive director and under-secretary general for the United Nations
a2346.name: Winnie Byanyima
a2346.title: UNAIDS executive director and under-secretary general for the United Nations
a2346.speech: Said there is now need to free domestic resources for investing in health.

a2346.speaker: Zambia National Broadcasting Corporation (news item)
a2346.name: Zambia National Broadcasting Corporation (news item)
a2346.speech: This is according to a news item monitored on the Zambia National Broadcasting Corporation last evening.

a2489.speaker: Department of Disaster Management Affairs (Dodma) (update/statement signed by Commissioner Charles Kalemba)
a2489.name: Department of Disaster Management Affairs (Dodma) (update/statement signed by Commissioner Charles Kalemba)
a2489.speech: Said in an update that 227 people have been displaced while the number of injured persons has also increased from 16 to 29, and that the number of affected households has risen from 7 721 to 10 159; the death toll from Cyclone Chido has reached 13 from seven reported on Tuesday.

a2489.speaker: Charles Kalemba, Dodma Commissioner
a2489.name: Charles Kalemba
a2489.title: Dodma Commissioner
a2489.speech: Clarified in an interview that the figures reported on Monday and Tuesday were preliminary while yesterday's report was the final one: "It means we have collected all the information that we needed to collect from councils."

a2489.speaker: Charles Kalemba, Dodma Commissioner
a2489.name: Charles Kalemba
a2489.title: Dodma Commissioner
a2489.speech: Said Dodma has not opened evacuation camps for the displaced people since they are staying with their relatives in their villages.

a2489.speaker: Charles Kalemba, Dodma Commissioner
a2489.name: Charles Kalemba
a2489.title: Dodma Commissioner
a2489.speech: On humanitarian assistance, said the needs are within Dodma's contingency plan and delivery of relief items in Southern Region districts was expected to be completed yesterday while Central Region districts will receive items today.

a2489.speaker: Martin Chiwanda, Machinga District Council spokesperson
a2489.name: Martin Chiwanda
a2489.title: Machinga District Council spokesperson
a2489.speech: Said in an interview that the district has recorded two deaths and five injuries with 557 households affected: "The people have received psychosocial support, but we are yet to provide them with food and other relief items as we are still mobilising the resources."

a2489.speaker: Faith Khamula, Blantyre District Council disaster risk management officer
a2489.name: Faith Khamula
a2489.title: Blantyre District Council disaster risk management officer
a2489.speech: Said the council has already started distributing a 50 kilogramme bag of maize to each of the affected 502 households in the district.

a2528.speaker: Thomas Musah Tanko, General Secretary of the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT)
a2528.name: Thomas Musah Tanko
a2528.title: General Secretary of the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT)
a2528.speech: “As a nation, we have lost character and conscience. We are now training people with knowledge, but when it comes to character and conscience, we have fallen short. If care is not taken, we will all be in trouble in the coming years. This is something policymakers must seriously address.”

a2528.speaker: John Milton, English poet
a2528.name: John Milton
a2528.title: English poet
a2528.speech: In his poem “Paradise Lost” of 1667 he invented the word “Pandemonium,” as the capital of Hell, describing Pandemonium as the “high capital of Satan and his peers!”

a2528.speaker: The Speaker of Parliament of Ghana
a2528.name: The Speaker of Parliament of Ghana
a2528.speech: On the first sitting of the 8th Parliament on January 15, 2021, the Speaker strongly reprimanded the MPs for their “unruly behaviour” and “despicable conduct!” He warned he would have none of that on his watch.

a2528.speaker: A venerable statesman (anonymous)
a2528.name: A venerable statesman (anonymous)
a2528.speech: opined that Parliament was now perceived as a goldmine where people went not to serve, but to make money.

a2528.speaker: Sam Okudzeto, elder statesman
a2528.name: Sam Okudzeto
a2528.title: elder statesman
a2528.speech: said “Ghana has become a nation of hooligans”.

a2528.speaker: Unnamed interlocutor in Uganda (anonymous)
a2528.name: Unnamed interlocutor in Uganda (anonymous)
a2528.speech: “When people know they can get away with murder because nothing will happen to them, they will kill with impunity. But when they know they will also be killed for murder because the Law works, they will not kill!”

a2730.speaker: Pharmaceutical suppliers (27 companies, objections to ESPPRA)
a2730.name: Pharmaceutical suppliers (27 companies
a2730.title: objections to ESPPRA)
a2730.speech: Submitted 19 objections to the Eswatini Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (ESPPRA), complaining about the handling of two government tenders with a total value of about E1 billion ; individually and collectively, the 27 companies cited possible bias and corruption in the award of the tenders.

a2730.speaker: One of the bidding companies (complaint to ESPPRA)
a2730.name: One of the bidding companies (complaint to ESPPRA)
a2730.speech: Complained about being disqualified from participating in Tender No.1 of 2025/2026 for the supply and delivery of medical supplies, having submitted a bid valued at over E123 million, and alleges that its disqualification from this lucrative tender was communicated without clarity, in violation of the principles of fairness and transparency enshrined in the Procurement Act.

a2730.speaker: Suppliers (unnamed)
a2730.name: Suppliers (unnamed)
a2730.speech: There is a feeling among suppliers that government’s approach towards the tendering process has changed, which raises “serious concerns regarding fairness and consistency in evaluation” of tenders.

a2730.speaker: Office of the Auditor General (Eswatini), audit report
a2730.name: Office of the Auditor General (Eswatini)
a2730.title: audit report
a2730.speech: Reported in his last report that medical drugs that were part of a consignment worth over E33 million had not been delivered to the Central Medical Stores (CMS).

a2730.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a2730.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a2730.title: President of South Africa
a2730.speech: Said on the first day of South Africa’s national dialogue that one of the pressing issues South Africa needed to address was why clinics ran out of medicine.

a2730.speaker: Health experts (South Africa)
a2730.name: Health experts (South Africa)
a2730.speech: Were quick with the retort that this particular question needed proper governance, not a national dialogue ; told journalists that medicine shortages were caused by poor management, lack of live budgeting, unqualified Members of the Executive Council (MECs), provincial distribution failures, budget constraints and external supply chain problems ; also cited brain drain, poor working conditions of health workers, mismanagement, and a lack of accountability and transparency in the health system ; it was stated that the MECs of health in the various provinces were not health professionals.

a2730.speaker: Newsday (report)
a2730.name: Newsday (report)
a2730.speech: Went on to state that the lack of essential health resources was a problem that had plagued South Africa for several years and was the leading cause of medical negligence; payouts for medical negligence claims reportedly increased by an average 23 per cent each year between 2014 and 2020.

a2730.speaker: Think Global Health (report)
a2730.name: Think Global Health (report)
a2730.speech: Revealed that clinical errors, mismanagement, lack of accountability, and inadequate facilities and equipment were primary causes of negligence in South Africa.

a2730.speaker: Neal Rijkenberg, Minister of Finance (Eswatini), Budget Speech
a2730.name: Neal Rijkenberg
a2730.title: Minister of Finance (Eswatini), Budget Speech
a2730.speech: Acknowledged what was then a 90-day pause in funding from the US, saying, “Fortunately, the US government recently re-instated limited portions of its funding for urgent lifesaving HIV care and treatment services” ; promised that they would continue to work closely with the US Embassy “during this difficult time.”

a2910.speaker: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), new projections (July 2025)
a2910.name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
a2910.title: new projections (July 2025)
a2910.speech: According to new OECD projections, official development assistance could fall by as much as 17% this year, continuing a trend already begun in 2024; the OECD anticipates a further fall in net aid in 2025 of between 9% and 17%, representing a loss of 56 billion dollars in just two years; bilateral aid to sub-Saharan Africa could decline by 16% to 28% in 2025, a return to mid-2000s levels; and the OECD estimates that health financing in sub-Saharan Africa could fall by a further 14% to 29% in 2025, after a 40% drop in 2023 and 6% in 2024, while humanitarian aid funding could fall by up to 36% between 2023 and 2025 and education resources by 18% to 22%.

a3069.speaker: Reinaldo Goncalves, keynote speaker of the panel at the 15th Session of the Tax Council of the Tax Authority (AT)
a3069.name: Reinaldo Goncalves
a3069.title: keynote speaker of the panel at the 15th Session of the Tax Council of the Tax Authority (AT)
