a3069.speech: Said that Mozambique has achieved immense gains with the implementation of the monthly Bulletin of Reference Prices (BMPR), which sets the reference prices of mineral products harmonised with international market reference prices, but that it can do more ; said that despite the progress the country still struggles with challenges in the sector, including the integrity and validation of the data declared in the tax assessment ; added that this requires the "education and training of the officials involved in taxation so that they have the technical capacity to assess and validate the quality of the material and consequently define its value", since currently it is the mining companies themselves that report the grade of their production.

a3069.speaker: Participants at the 15th Session of the Tax Council of the Tax Authority
a3069.name: Participants at the 15th Session of the Tax Council of the Tax Authority
a3069.speech: Advocate the training of technical staff from other areas, including the AT, customs, and the Police of the Republic of Mozambique (PRM), who "often fail to carry out certain tasks because they do not know the value of the minerals".

a3069.speaker: Katia Murgy, Coordinator of the Extractive Industry Taxation Unit at the Tax Authority (AT)
a3069.name: Katia Murgy
a3069.title: Coordinator of the Extractive Industry Taxation Unit at the Tax Authority (AT)
a3069.speech: Emphasises that the establishment of reference prices guarantees tax equity and fairness, while recognising that the BMPR is not finished, hence its monthly updating for adjustments towards correct application ; highlights the importance of improving the control of mineral exports and the certification of their quality (through the establishment of laboratories and refineries) to guarantee improved taxation according to their grade, which is volatile.

a3069.speaker: Angelo Macuacua, participant in the event
a3069.name: Angelo Macuacua
a3069.title: participant in the event
a3069.speech: Said that there must be "quality control of the minerals through independent inspection at the site of extraction of the mineral resources, by means of a system that transmits data [on mineral quality] in real time to the tax management system".

a3069.speaker: Gracio Cune, moderator of the panel
a3069.name: Gracio Cune
a3069.title: moderator of the panel
a3069.speech: Said the National Institute of the Sea (INAMAR), the maritime authority, must step up its action, explaining that "it is very important for the mineral resources sector and perhaps surpasses the AT, because what is taxed passes first through the hands of INAMAR, which receives and dispatches the ships carrying the goods".

a3103.speaker: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, Brazilian President
a3103.name: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva
a3103.title: Brazilian President
a3103.speech: Urged his French counterpart Emmanuel Macron to “finalise” an EU trade deal with four South American countries: “Open your heart a little to this opportunity to finalise this agreement with our dear Mercosur.” ; “This agreement would be the strongest response our regions could offer in the face of the uncertainty caused by the return of unilateralism and tariff protectionism.”

a3103.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3103.name: Donald Trump
a3103.title: US President
a3103.speech: Argues that his tariffs will bring manufacturing jobs back to the United States.

a3103.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a3103.name: Emmanuel Macron
a3103.title: French President
a3103.speech: Reiterated his concerns about the deal’s impact on French farmers, citing differences in environmental regulations between the EU and Mercosur countries: “I don’t know how to explain to my farmers that, at a time when I am asking them to comply with more standards, I am opening up my market on a massive scale to people who do not comply at all.” ; “Because what will happen? It won’t be better for the climate, but we will completely destroy our agriculture.” ; “That is why I said earlier we must improve this deal.”

a3103.speaker: Agriculture ministers from France, Hungary and Austria (joint statement)
a3103.name: Agriculture ministers from France
a3103.title: Hungary and Austria (joint statement)
a3103.speech: Reiterated their “strong concerns” about the accord, which they consider “imbalanced to the detriment of European agricultural interests”.

a3103.speaker: France (government)
a3103.name: France (government)
a3103.speech: Has said from the start the Mercosur deal is not acceptable in its current form.

a3103.speaker: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, Brazilian President
a3103.name: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva
a3103.title: Brazilian President
a3103.speech: Accused Israel of carrying out “premeditated genocide” in the Palestinian territory of Gaza: “(It is) a premeditated genocide from a far-right government that is waging a war against the interests of its own people.”

a3103.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a3103.name: Emmanuel Macron
a3103.title: French President
a3103.speech: Has refused to use the term “genocide”, saying last month it was not for a “political leader to use the term but up to historians to do so when the time comes”.

a3103.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a3103.name: Emmanuel Macron
a3103.title: French President
a3103.speech: Said that he expected the UN conference in New York would take steps “towards recognising Palestine”, without being more specific.

a3103.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a3103.name: Emmanuel Macron
a3103.title: French President
a3103.speech: Stressed that Kyiv and Moscow should not be treated as equals: “There is an aggressor, which is Russia. There is a victim, which is Ukraine. We all want peace, but we cannot treat the two belligerents equally,” stressing that Brazil had “a very important role to play” in finding a solution to the conflict.

a3103.speaker: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, Brazilian President
a3103.name: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva
a3103.title: Brazilian President
a3103.speech: Said he hoped to reinforce Brazil’s ties with Russia during his May 9 trip to Moscow: “My visit here is to strengthen and rebuild our strategic partnership.”

a3103.speaker: European Union
a3103.name: European Union
a3103.speech: Warned its members not to travel to Moscow for the event.

a3428.speaker: John Legend, American singer-songwriter
a3428.name: John Legend
a3428.title: American singer-songwriter
a3428.speech: Told the BBC he is unfazed by a public backlash against his decision to perform in Rwanda: "I don't believe that we should punish the people of Rwanda and punish the people of other countries when we disagree with their leaders." ; "I'm aware of what's happening [in DR Congo] and I'm aware of the calls there have been for me to not do this show, but I really believe that the mission of Move Afrika is still important."

a3428.speaker: John Legend, American singer-songwriter
a3428.name: John Legend
a3428.title: American singer-songwriter
a3428.speech: Said he was not being paid for the performance but felt it was his duty to help "grow touring capabilities" on the African continent, which is often overlooked by international stars on so-called world tours.

a3428.speaker: Tems, Grammy-winning singer
a3428.name: Tems
a3428.title: Grammy-winning singer
a3428.speech: Pulled out of a concert she was due to give on Saturday in Rwanda, saying she would "never, ever intend to be insensitive to real-world issues".

a3428.speaker: Denise Zanesa, Belgium-based activist (post on X)
a3428.name: Denise Zanesa
a3428.title: Belgium-based activist (post on X)
a3428.speech: Argued that "performing under the banner" of Rwanda "would be akin to collaborating with oppression itself".

a3428.speaker: Simone Umba, in the US (TikTok video caption)
a3428.name: Simone Umba
a3428.title: in the US (TikTok video caption)
a3428.speech: "So are we ready to talk about Rwanda's use of Black American culture in their soft campaigning to normalise their terrorising of eastern Congo?"

a3428.speaker: John Legend's aide (non-response)
a3428.name: John Legend's aide (non-response)
a3428.speech: When asked Legend's thoughts on the sportswashing topic, Legend's aide told the BBC that he would not answer that question.

a3436.speaker: Governments at the Tokyo International Conference on African Development (TICAD)
a3436.name: Governments at the Tokyo International Conference on African Development (TICAD)
a3436.speech: Agreed that sanitation was a fundamental element of human capital development.

a3468.speaker: National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) (letter)
a3468.name: National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) (letter)
a3468.speech: The Bank started transferring the foreign currency to the Ethiopian Shipping & Logistics Services Enterprise last month following a letter from the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE).

a3468.speaker: Roba Megersa, CEO of the Ethiopian Shipping & Logistics Services Enterprise
a3468.name: Roba Megersa
a3468.title: CEO of the Ethiopian Shipping & Logistics Services Enterprise
a3468.speech: “Out of our total demand of foreign currency,” said Roba Megersa, CEO of the Enterprise, “we get only 30pc of it.” ; “Due to the forex crunch,” said Roba, “we're unable to settle outstanding payments for services we receive.”

a3468.speaker: Roba Megersa, CEO of the Ethiopian Shipping & Logistics Services Enterprise
a3468.name: Roba Megersa
a3468.title: CEO of the Ethiopian Shipping & Logistics Services Enterprise
a3468.speech: Explained that the central bank made the intervention to ensure that the two commodities — wheat and fertiliser — were delivered on time ; said that once the wheat and the fertiliser are fully transported into the country, the 25-million-dollar allocation from the CBE will be stopped.

a3468.speaker: Officials at the central bank and the commercial bank (non-response)
a3468.name: Officials at the central bank and the commercial bank (non-response)
a3468.speech: Officials at the central bank and the commercial bank were not immediately available for comment.

a3580.speaker: National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3580.name: National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3580.speech: says 19.2 million citizens have enrolled on health insurance schemes surpassing its 2024 target.

a3580.speaker: Kelechi Ohiri, Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3580.name: Kelechi Ohiri
a3580.title: Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3580.speech: disclosed that 19.2 million citizens have enrolled on health insurance schemes; said this feat was a significant milestone in the NHIA's efforts to expand access to healthcare for Nigerians under the health insurance scheme, that the achievement surpasses the 2024 target and places the nation at 95 per cent of its ambitious 2027 presidential coverage goal, and attributed the success to strategic policy reforms, effective collaborations with stakeholders, and an unwavering commitment to universal health coverage: "We are proud to announce that 19.2 million Nigerians have been covered by health insurance. This surpasses our 2024 target and places us within striking distance of achieving 95 per cent of the 2027 presidential target."

a3580.speaker: Kelechi Ohiri, Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3580.name: Kelechi Ohiri
a3580.title: Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3580.speech: said that the NHIA had worked tirelessly to implement innovative strategies: "This includes the expansion of the Basic Healthcare Provision Fund (BHCPF) and partnerships with state health insurance agencies to ensure affordable and accessible healthcare for all Nigerians, especially the most vulnerable populations." ; said the milestone reflects the federal government's commitment to delivering quality healthcare as outlined in the National Health Act.

a3580.speaker: Kelechi Ohiri, Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3580.name: Kelechi Ohiri
a3580.title: Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3580.speech: urged state governments and private sector stakeholders to intensify efforts to sustain the momentum and bridge the remaining gaps in health insurance coverage.

a3580.speaker: Kelechi Ohiri, Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3580.name: Kelechi Ohiri
a3580.title: Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3580.speech: said that the achievement came amid ongoing challenges in Nigeria's healthcare sector, including funding limitations, infrastructure deficits, and inadequate human resources, but expressed optimism, noting that the agency's strategic roadmap for 2025-2027 includes scaling up digital enrollment processes and integrating informal sector workers into the insurance scheme.

a3580.speaker: Kelechi Ohiri, Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3580.name: Kelechi Ohiri
a3580.title: Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3580.speech: "With the theme of this year's UHC Day, health should reflect the type of government the country has and must make decisions that represent its aspirations. We should prioritise Primary Health Care (PHC) as the bedrock of our health system."

a3580.speaker: Muhammad Lawal, Commissioner for Health in Yobe
a3580.name: Muhammad Lawal
a3580.title: Commissioner for Health in Yobe
a3580.speech: said that UHC was a reality and we must work towards it ; said that there should be no negotiation for the health of the people, especially the vulnerable segment of the population.

a3580.speaker: Bolanle Olusola-Faleye, USAID LHSS Project
a3580.name: Bolanle Olusola-Faleye
a3580.title: USAID LHSS Project
a3580.speech: said that it was a remarkable time to celebrate 2024 UHC Day with the presence of reforms such as the Sector Wide Approach (SWAP) ; said that SWAP had shown evidence of success in the states through the harmonised Annual Operational Plan (AOP), ensuring alignment of priorities.

a3580.speaker: Public health advocates
a3580.name: Public health advocates
a3580.speech: have lauded the progress, describing it as a significant step toward achieving UHC in Nigeria.

a3580.speaker: Garfa Alawode, Co-convener of the UHC2023 Forum
a3580.name: Garfa Alawode
a3580.title: Co-convener of the UHC2023 Forum
a3580.speech: said that it was a commendable accomplishment; however, said that more needed to be done to ensure that every Nigerian could access affordable, quality healthcare services, and called for sustained political will, increased funding, and effective monitoring: "This is to ensure that the gains are not only maintained but also translated into improved health outcomes for all citizens."

a3580.speaker: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a3580.name: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a3580.speech: reports that the roundtable was part of the activities lined up for the commemoration of the 2024 UHC Day ; recalls that UHC Day is a global advocacy day to raise awareness about the importance of equitable, affordable, and accessible healthcare for all individuals without financial hardship.

a3654.speaker: Edouard Sehlin, director general of the Agency for the Development of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (ADPME)
a3654.name: Edouard Sehlin
a3654.title: director general of the Agency for the Development of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (ADPME)
a3654.speech: According to him, the ADPME is tasked with informing, advising, supporting and guiding micro, small and medium-sized enterprises towards existing support mechanisms, assisting with their categorisation, helping them seize opportunities and supporting high-potential enterprises ; “It may involve capacity building, advice, diagnosis or networking, and facilitating access to financing” ; explains that in terms of financing the Agency plays a catalytic role in order to encourage financial actors to intervene in market segments, or categories of enterprises, in which they are not sufficiently present.

a3654.speaker: Modeste Tihounté Kérékou, Minister of SMEs and Employment Promotion
a3654.name: Modeste Tihounté Kérékou
a3654.title: Minister of SMEs and Employment Promotion
a3654.speech: According to him, the PAG 2016-2021 amounted to around 9,038 billion CFA francs, with the intention of generating 500,000 direct and indirect jobs ; “We were already at more than 600,000 direct and indirect jobs more than a year before the end of the term. The PAG 2021-2026 is 12,011 billion F CFA and 1,300,000 jobs that the government intends to create in close cooperation with the private sector. That is why a good part of the reforms completed in the first term have continued, and their effects are increasingly evident” ; cites in particular the facilitation of business creation and the legislative framework put in place through the investment code, the law on the promotion of SMEs, and the law on hiring procedures in the Republic of Benin.

a3654.speaker: Edouard Sehlin, director of the Agency for the Development of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (ADPME)
a3654.name: Edouard Sehlin
a3654.title: director of the Agency for the Development of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (ADPME)
a3654.speech: “All the projects planned in the SME sector have been finalised and are starting up with all the partners. We will do more, because this makes it possible to have an impact and to have a critical mass of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises capable of contributing to the structural transformation of the economy and ensuring Benin's prosperity in the future...”

a3654.speaker: Urbain Amégbédji, director general of the National Employment Agency (ANPE)
a3654.name: Urbain Amégbédji
a3654.title: director general of the National Employment Agency (ANPE)
a3654.speech: “The government has provided us with new tools that make it possible to promote employment more effectively and efficiently, notably the Special Programme for Integration into Employment (PSIE), which became effective in 2020 and which today reaches about 3,000 young people working in companies, whose salaries and all charges are covered by the State” ; assures that through the PSIE it is support both for the enterprise and for the professional integration of young people, with much greater efficiency than in the past ; explains that the youth inclusion project makes it possible, in on average 6 months, to train and put to work a young person who can immediately obtain a contract and start working.

a3654.speaker: Modeste Kérékou, Minister of SMEs and Employment Promotion
a3654.name: Modeste Kérékou
a3654.title: Minister of SMEs and Employment Promotion
a3654.speech: “We have an organisation of the crafts world that has been completely overhauled so that it complies not only with the law but also with the provisions of the community code of the UEMOA area” ; adds that, in place of the old structure, a chamber of trades has been enshrined in law, endowed with a consular Assembly made up of 80 members elected by their peers, drawn from 164 trades in accordance with the UEMOA crafts nomenclature, namely 40 trade bodies and eight branches of activity.

a3654.speaker: Robert N'Dah Sinkeni, director of crafts
a3654.name: Robert N'Dah Sinkeni
a3654.title: director of crafts
a3654.speech: “The Chamber of Crafts Trades has as its essential mission to represent the sector before the public authorities and any other body, to defend the interests of artisans, and to work for the promotion of the sector.”

a3846.speaker: Olavo Correia, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance of Cabo Verde
a3846.name: Olavo Correia
a3846.title: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance of Cabo Verde
a3846.speech: Announced that the third Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) compact will prioritise connectivity and mobility across several dimensions - land, air, maritime, digital and human.

a3954.speaker: US Ambassador to the Republic of Tanzania (opinion piece / farewell message)
a3954.name: US Ambassador to the Republic of Tanzania (opinion piece / farewell message)
a3954.speech: “AS I depart Tanzania, I want to thank each and every Tanzanian for welcoming me and my wife Linda to your beautiful country” ; said that since their arrival in January of 2023 there have been many highlights over the past two years, including Vice-President Kamala Harris’s visit early in his tenure, which paved the way for the signing of the US-Tanzania Commercial Dialogue bringing the US and Tanzanian public and private sectors together to increase bilateral trade and investment ; noted that last month President Biden travelled to Angola, where he met with Vice-President Mpango alongside other regional heads of state to discuss continued development of the Trans-Africa Continental Railroad, a project in which the United States is a major investor.

a3954.speaker: US Ambassador to the Republic of Tanzania (opinion piece / farewell message)
a3954.name: US Ambassador to the Republic of Tanzania (opinion piece / farewell message)
a3954.speech: Said that, recognising that strong economies and strong democracies go hand-in-hand, he was proud to deliver additional assistance to strengthen the development of Tanzania’s health, education, democratic governance and economic growth systems, and that he had the privilege of meeting beneficiaries of US-funded programmes in his many travels around Tanzania.

a3954.speaker: US Ambassador to the Republic of Tanzania (opinion piece / farewell message)
a3954.name: US Ambassador to the Republic of Tanzania (opinion piece / farewell message)
a3954.speech: “I often say that the greatest asset Tanzania has is not its gold, nor its Tanzanite, nor even its abundant wildlife and natural beauty. Rather, the greatest asset Tanzania has is its people” ; said spending time with Tanzania’s inspiring youth has been by far one of the great highlights of his tenure as Ambassador, citing the Youth Democracy Dialogues supported by a U.S. embassy grant in August of 2023, ensuring more Tanzanians have access to high-quality education in US universities, the U.S.-Tanzania Tech Challenge to which over 100 tech innovators submitted proposals, and advocacy to bring a Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) Threshold project back to Tanzania.

a3954.speaker: US Ambassador to the Republic of Tanzania (opinion piece / farewell message)
a3954.name: US Ambassador to the Republic of Tanzania (opinion piece / farewell message)
a3954.speech: Said he has continued to speak out both publicly and privately in support of the continued development of Tanzania’s democracy, because a mature Tanzanian democratic governance will not only make Tanzania freer and fairer but also wealthier ; said that is why the United States is Tanzania’s largest development partner and will continue to invest in strengthening the health sector, reducing deaths and improving the quality of life of tens of millions of Tanzanians, supporting those living with HIV/AIDS through PEPFAR.

a3954.speaker: US Ambassador to the Republic of Tanzania (opinion piece / farewell message)
a3954.name: US Ambassador to the Republic of Tanzania (opinion piece / farewell message)
a3954.speech: “I remain impressed by the shared dedication Tanzanians have to the principles of umoja, utu and ushirikiano. A united Tanzania, committed to the ideals of respecting every citizen’s human dignity is a Tanzania that will positively impact the world. That was the dream of Mwalimu Nyerere and a dream I will keep in my heart long after leaving Tanzania” ; “It has been the honour of my lifetime to serve as the U.S. Ambassador to Tanzania.”

a3999.speaker: Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe
a3999.name: Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe
a3999.speech: Says there was a decline in the country's foreign currency inflows during the first half of 2023, as the surge in metal prices that followed the onset of the Russia-Ukraine conflict eases.

a3999.speaker: John Mangudya, Governor of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe
a3999.name: John Mangudya
a3999.title: Governor of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe
a3999.speech: In his mid-term monetary policy statement last week, reported “a transitory decline…”

a4055.speaker: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)
a4055.name: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)
a4055.speech: warned on Tuesday that global funding cuts could force a further 6 million children to drop out of school by the end of next year.

a4055.speaker: Institute for Security Studies (ISS) (study)
a4055.name: Institute for Security Studies (ISS) (study)
a4055.speech: research indicated today that the suspension of the activities of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) may increase the risk of human rights violations, notably in Mozambique.

a4578.speaker: Governments at the Tokyo International Conference on African Development
a4578.name: Governments at the Tokyo International Conference on African Development
a4578.speech: Agreed that sanitation was a fundamental element of human capital development.

a4578.speaker: Samuel Langat, General Manager for SATO (LIXIL)
a4578.name: Samuel Langat
a4578.title: General Manager for SATO (LIXIL)
a4578.speech: "At LIXIL, we're committed to building on and expanding our work on the continent... We fully support the greater alignment of stakeholders and coherence on promoting universal health coverage, and we will continue to play our part with local partners in the sanitation field. We call on new partners to join us in tackling this crisis."

a4925.speaker: Trigon Metals (company statement)
a4925.name: Trigon Metals (company statement)
a4925.speech: Said that at the Kombat mine, May was marked by several record-breaking underground mining days, leading to a production average of 12.1 tonnes of copper per day; acknowledged its dedicated Namibian team for this outstanding achievement ; reported that further to the announcement of commercial production from its underground mine on 23 May, the underground mine had continued to perform and exceed the production targets defined in its feasibility study ; said its focus for the financial year 2025 remains on underground production from the Asis West underground complex, with underground production expected to amount to between 250 000 and 280 000 ore tonnes mined for the financial year at an average grade of between 1.95% and 2.3% copper, copper metal production projected between 5 500 and 6 100 tonnes, and cash costs expected to average between US$2.80/pound and US$3.15/pound ; said production from the underground averaged 552 tonnes per day by April and produced more than 1 000 tonnes per day on four occasions in May ; said dewatering continues at a rate of 2 800 cubic metres an hour against an in-flow rate of 1 200 cubic metres an hour, the mine now dewatered to 315 metres below shaft collar, and assured that back-up power capacity is in place to ensure an uninterrupted power supply for underground pump systems.

a4925.speaker: Rennie Morkel, Trigon president and chief operating officer
a4925.name: Rennie Morkel
a4925.title: Trigon president and chief operating officer
a4925.speech: “We are exceptionally pleased with the accelerated ramp-up of the underground mine and thank our Namibian team for their hard work and ongoing efforts at Kombat” ; “Our strategy for the upcoming fiscal year is focused on maximising underground production from the current mining areas as well as to ensure that we are establishing ourselves for the next phases of our growth trajectory, both at Asis West and in terms of the planned restart of Asis Far West” ; “Congratulations to our homegrown owner-operated underground mining teams. Re-asserting Kombat as an underground copper producing mine is a tremendous achievement for the operation, the company and our community. Going forward, we will look for opportunities to grow production from underground, which - in turn - should increase our copper production and our profitability. My sincerest appreciation to the entire Kombat team, under the guidance of our vice-president of operations, Fanie Muller, for their tireless efforts in achieving this important milestone for the future of Kombat”.

a4925.speaker: Knowledge Katti, entrepreneur, owner of Texel Mining and Exploration (10% stake in the Kombat mine)
a4925.name: Knowledge Katti
a4925.title: entrepreneur, owner of Texel Mining and Exploration (10% stake in the Kombat mine)
a4925.speech: “We are delighted at the vindication of our tireless journey, which started on a bumpy note a decade ago. This unprecedented level of performance is already competitively contributing to the Namibian economy and touching thousands of Namibian lives positively” ; “We consider our government a key stakeholder and our continued appeal is for improved investment in basic infrastructure in and around Kombat, which has become a budding locality thanks to the ongoing successful mining activity. The spin-offs of such state interventions would be invaluable to the local community”.

a4925.speaker: Jeremy Hangula, Local director at Trigon Namibia
a4925.name: Jeremy Hangula
a4925.title: Local director at Trigon Namibia
a4925.speech: “We are excited about the ever-improving production outcomes and the positive prospects for the year ahead. This is all down to the tireless efforts of our employees at the mine”.

a4925.speaker: Jed Richardson, CEO and executive chairman of Trigon Metals
a4925.name: Jed Richardson
a4925.title: CEO and executive chairman of Trigon Metals
a4925.speech: “Increased grade from underground has profoundly impacted our metal production, making each tonne more profitable. It has improved recovery in the mill and increased the grade of the concentrate. The Kombat mine has been primarily an underground mine through its 45-year history. Our experience is now showing us why”.

a5181.speaker: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.name: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.speech: On why an extraordinary Board meeting was held: “Benin's Millennium Challenge Account Programme is of capital importance for the Government. Today we are in the active phase of this Programme and there are extremely important works to be carried out at the Port of Cotonou within the framework of the ‘Access to Markets’ Project... the Grant Agreement provides that any disbursement of more than one hundred million US dollars must be approved by the Board of Directors. That is why we have today convened the Board of Directors in extraordinary session to take this decision.”

a5181.speaker: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.name: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.speech: On the lots awarded: said the major works at the port of Cotonou have been divided into six lots, of which lots 1 and 2 are already awarded and lot 3's process is under way, and that “all arrangements have been made so that we can have a good result and stay within the deadline”, with the Board working alongside the National Coordinator.

a5181.speaker: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.name: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.speech: On the rate of fund use: “We are entering the process with a very high level of use starting from the port component, and this component alone accounted for around 60% of the whole Programme. I think that with the signing of the contracts, which will take place at the latest next week, we will surely find ourselves at 80 or 85% use of the 307 million US dollars allocated by the United States of America.”

a5181.speaker: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.name: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.speech: On whether the Programme is ending: “The end! No. I would like us to be able to speak of the end only when we have fully committed the funds allocated to the Programme... beyond these lots 1, 2 and 3 there are three other lots that are very important for the modernisation of our port.”

a5181.speaker: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.name: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.speech: On doubts that the $307 million would be used before the 2011 deadline: “I can assure you that the budget will be used up. I said the last time that if the United States of America could grant us a further supplement, we would not say no, because beyond everything that has been planned, we have many other projects within the framework of the modernisation of the port... But I am convinced that we will of course use up the entirety of the funds placed at our disposal.” ; “The Beninese government is determined to use up the entirety of the funds allocated to MCA-Benin so that on the evening of 05 October 2011, not one penny is returned to the Americans.”

a5181.speaker: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.name: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.speech: On projects dragging their feet: “I am a man of conviction. Since I took office, every day that God grants, alongside the National Coordinator, we move things forward. No project is dragging its feet any longer, I can assure you.”

a5181.speaker: Lee Roussel, Resident Director of MCC (reported by the Chairman)
a5181.name: Lee Roussel
a5181.title: Resident Director of MCC (reported by the Chairman)
a5181.speech: Said a few words concerning two ministries: she gave him to understand that it would not be judicious for the Minister of Finance, the principal agent, to also sit on the Board of Directors; and MCC thinks that the Minister of Development, Minister of State, cannot be a member of the Board of Directors while the Chairman of the Board is not a Minister of State.

a5181.speaker: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.name: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.speech: On ministers' participation in the board: said the question should be put to the government, which expressed the wish that the directors be the ministers themselves, and that what the Head of State seeks through this representation is the effectiveness of the board of directors and the happy outcome of the programme. “He has always said that this Programme is a Programme of Benin. The United States of America has placed at Benin's disposal a fund for the modernisation of its economy in general and it is normal that this fund should be used efficiently.”

a5181.speaker: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.name: Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin
a5181.speech: In conclusion: thanked the National Coordination, the Resident Director of MCC and the journalists, said “in general we congratulate ourselves on the agreements that exist between the United States and Benin”, renewed the commitment that all of the fund be used up, and urged citizens to be patient during the works at the Port of Cotonou: “A modern port interests everyone, it suits everyone.”

a5260.speaker: Antonin Dossou, Chief of Staff of the Ministry in charge of Development (Benin)
a5260.name: Antonin Dossou
a5260.title: Chief of Staff of the Ministry in charge of Development (Benin)
a5260.speech: Presented, at a meeting with the media on Thursday 28 May 2010 in Cotonou, the "Delivering as One" reform initiated by the UN Secretary-General, which Benin aspires to implement ; Indicated that the "Delivering as One" reform rests on four pillars, namely: a single programme, a single budgetary framework, a single leader, a single office, pillars supported by a single communication strategy and a single monitoring and evaluation system ; Said the stakes of "Delivering as One" for Benin lie among other things in its greater effectiveness compared with the fragmented mode of intervention that previously existed, and in the easier alignment of the agencies' activities with the country's Programme-Budget by relying on the common programme.

a5260.speaker: Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Benin
a5260.name: Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Benin
a5260.speech: Assisted the Chief of Staff of the Ministry in charge of Development in presenting the "Delivering as One" reform initiated by the Secretary-General of the United Nations to the media.

a5317.speaker: LBS reporter (William Howard)
a5317.name: LBS reporter (William Howard)
a5317.speech: "Citizens have welcomed the initiative, considering it a great step toward sustainable development."

a5317.speaker: Citizens of Central Monrovia
a5317.name: Citizens of Central Monrovia
a5317.speech: Believe that road construction is paramount to the country, and as such are urging their counterparts to cooperate with the two ministries for the development of the nation.

a5391.speaker: Alassane Séidou, Minister of Health of Benin
a5391.name: Alassane Séidou
a5391.title: Minister of Health of Benin
a5391.speech: reiterated the Government's determination to fight malaria in Benin; explains, backed by recent statistics from his ministry, that there is truly an urgent need not to weaken in the response against this disease; according to him, malaria remains, at 42.8%, the leading cause of recourse to care in health facilities and the leading cause of hospitalisation at 52.3%, pregnant women and children under five being the most vulnerable, and the leading cause of death in health facilities with an incidence of 14.6% ; “This naturally dreadful rate shows that despite the efforts made, malaria remains a public health problem.”

a5391.speaker: Alassane Séidou, Minister of Health of Benin
a5391.name: Alassane Séidou
a5391.title: Minister of Health of Benin
a5391.speech: thanks the Global Fund and the American Government, through the President's Malaria Initiative (PMI), for having contributed a large share to the mobilisation of these insecticide-treated nets ; invited every head of household who was counted during the enumeration phase to report to the post indicated in his neighbourhood with his coupon to collect his batch of mosquito nets ; issued an appeal to the entire population, to local elected officials and to law enforcement so that this distribution phase runs without obstacles ; urged the beneficiaries to make good use of the nets to guarantee their effectiveness.

a5391.speaker: Dr Jean-Pierre Baptiste, WHO resident representative in Benin
a5391.name: Dr Jean-Pierre Baptiste
a5391.title: WHO resident representative in Benin
a5391.speech: salutes the commitment of the Beninese Government to fight malaria; stresses that by this choice Benin gives itself not only the means to significantly reduce maternal and infant mortality, but also to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

a5391.speaker: Pilar Valasquez Gallega, representative of the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria
a5391.name: Pilar Valasquez Gallega
a5391.title: representative of the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria
a5391.speech: gives assurance of her institution's support to accompany Benin in the framework of the fight against this pandemic.

a5391.speaker: Joachim Apithy, prefect of Ouémé, and Eugène Lonégnon, mayor of Avrankou
a5391.name: Joachim Apithy
a5391.title: prefect of Ouémé, and Eugène Lonégnon, mayor of Avrankou
a5391.speech: promised to do everything in their power to guarantee the proper use of these mosquito nets so that they do not serve the population as fishing nets or as protective objects in plantations, notably market-garden crops.

a5617.speaker: Freedom Flotilla Coalition (FFC) (Telegram and social media posts)
a5617.name: Freedom Flotilla Coalition (FFC) (Telegram and social media posts)
a5617.speech: activists on board the Madleen say they have been intercepted by Israeli soldiers; posting on Telegram, the FFC announced “connection has been lost” on the Madleen and later uploaded a photo of people sitting with their hands up in life jackets ; said the situation caused panic and led many of them to take cover and put on life jackets in preparation for an intervention: “Alarm has been sounded on the Madleen. Life jackets are on, preparing for interception.”

a5617.speaker: Israel’s foreign ministry
a5617.name: Israel’s foreign ministry
a5617.speech: latest updates on the aid boat said the yacht was “safely making its way to the shores of Israel,” and its occupants were “expected to return to their home countries” ; released a video on X showing its navy giving orders to the Gaza-bound aid ship to divert and posted another footage that showed passengers of what it called the “Selfie Yacht” safe and unharmed.

a5617.speaker: Francesca Albanese, UN Special Rapporteur on occupied territories
a5617.name: Francesca Albanese
a5617.title: UN Special Rapporteur on occupied territories
a5617.speech: who claimed to be in contact with the flotilla’s communication room in Catania, noted that around five vessels had been circling the aid boat, with two drones hovering over the vessel ; posted on X: “BREAKING 1AM UK time. Israeli speedboat reached Madleen. ‘At the time the boat was intercepted no one is wounded’ the captain asked me to record. I heard the soldiers speaking while the captain was on the phone with me. I lost connection with the captain as he was telling me that…”

a5617.speaker: Israel Katz, Israeli Defence Minister
a5617.name: Israel Katz
a5617.title: Israeli Defence Minister
a5617.speech: said on Sunday that Israel wouldn’t allow anyone to break its naval blockade of the Palestinian territory, which he said was aimed at preventing Hamas from importing arms: “To the antisemitic Greta and her fellow Hamas propagandists — I will say this clearly: You should turn back, because you will not make it to Gaza.”

a5617.speaker: Freedom Flotilla Coalition (FFC)
a5617.name: Freedom Flotilla Coalition (FFC)
a5617.speech: blamed on Israel the May drone attack that damaged the frontal part of one of the group’s ships in international waters off Malta.

a5617.speaker: Israel
a5617.name: Israel
a5617.speech: strongly refuted the claim that it was responsible for the May drone attack on the group’s ship.

a5763.speaker: Local processors (Malian oilseed processors)
a5763.name: Local processors (Malian oilseed processors)
a5763.speech: Welcome the decision taken by the authorities to temporarily suspend the export of certain oilseed products from Mali

a5763.speaker: Kancou Keita Cissé, director of Mali-Shi, the first industrial shea-nut processing unit in Mali
a5763.name: Kancou Keita Cissé
a5763.title: director of Mali-Shi, the first industrial shea-nut processing unit in Mali
a5763.speech: “The temporary suspension of the export of shea nuts is a decision that favours the country’s industrial development. This measure encourages local processors to increase their production capacity and to promote job creation all along the value chain” ; considers that the decision “makes it possible to retain a greater share of the wealth generated by this sector within the national economy,” specifying that the resource is developed locally through the production of shea butter and press cake ; “This suspension represents an opportunity to secure the supply of raw materials, because until now the plant has not managed to produce at full capacity” ; said her company has a processing capacity of 30,000 tonnes of shea nuts per year, allowing production of about 12,000 tonnes of shea butter, and undertook to maximise this opportunity by strengthening local partnerships, increasing production and adding value to every component of the nut

a5763.speaker: Boubacar Sidiki Diabaté, secretary general of the National Federation of Oil and Animal Feed Producers of Mali
a5763.name: Boubacar Sidiki Diabaté
a5763.title: secretary general of the National Federation of Oil and Animal Feed Producers of Mali
a5763.speech: Indicates that the federation uses the entire seed production of the Malian Company for Textile Development (CMDT) and imports about 350,000 tonnes from Brazil ; “The oil we produce does not cover the population’s consumption needs. Every year we see that the market is flooded with oil coming from anywhere. During my trip to Brazil on behalf of my federation, I studied the possibilities of diversification in order to replicate those models in Mali. In this period of insecurity, however, follow-up is complicated” ; stresses that his organisation produces between 40 and 50 million litres of oil per year: “The State has organised two workshops to encourage actors to diversify their products. Some are currently testing soya, groundnut and even shea nut. We need a structure to supervise these sectors, as the CMDT does for cotton seed,” recalling that the export of cotton seed has been banned in Mali for more than a decade

a5763.speaker: Soumaila Coulibaly, president of the sesame sector
a5763.name: Soumaila Coulibaly
a5763.title: president of the sesame sector
a5763.speech: States that this ban gives concrete form to a long-standing demand of agricultural actors whose vision is focused on developing production, processing and marketing by producing higher-quality goods at lower cost ; “We discussed preserving the gains of the sesame sector, particularly with regard to price. With the price set at 600 CFA francs, we hope to maintain producers’ interest” ; insists on the importance of collaboration between the actors of the value chain, from production to storage, through to processing and marketing, in order to maximise the benefits for the country

a5763.speaker: Abdoulaye Konaté, president of the Ouolofobougou market
a5763.name: Abdoulaye Konaté
a5763.title: president of the Ouolofobougou market
a5763.speech: Believes that through this decision the authorities wish to promote local processing and guarantee an adequate supply to the factories, but argues that certain varieties of groundnuts, such as those intended for oil, should be processed locally while others, such as fresh groundnuts, should be allowed to be exported: “Groundnuts provide a living for thousands of people in Mali. We think the factories cannot absorb the entire production. Export is therefore essential, even for the State.”

a5763.speaker: Zédion Dembélé, Director General of Commerce, Consumption and Competition (DGCC)
a5763.name: Zédion Dembélé
a5763.title: Director General of Commerce, Consumption and Competition (DGCC)
a5763.speech: Explained at the signing of the protocol on the suspension decision that the main objective is to ensure the commitment of local units to buy the available stocks: “Once raw material needs are covered, the surpluses may be exported” ; said the measure will make edible oil accessible to the population at affordable prices and on a continuous basis

a5792.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5792.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5792.title: President of Ghana
a5792.speech: Emphasized the need for Africa to become more self-reliant, particularly in food production, as external aid sources become increasingly uncertain; referenced the decision by USAID to reduce aid to the continent, warning that African nations must take proactive measures to secure their own future: “We cannot continue to depend on aid indefinitely. The recent cuts in USAID support should be a wake-up call for Africa to strengthen its agricultural sector and food production systems. We have the land, the human resources, and the potential to achieve food security on our own terms” ; underscored the importance of investment in mechanized farming, improved irrigation systems, and intra-African trade to ensure long-term sustainability in food supply.

a5792.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5792.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5792.title: President of Ghana
a5792.speech: Highlighted the growing threat of climate change, stressing that Africa is already experiencing severe consequences despite contributing minimally to global emissions, and called for urgent global action to support vulnerable nations while urging African governments to take adaptive measures: “Climate change is not a distant threat—it is already affecting our agriculture, water supply, and overall economic stability. We need global cooperation to address this crisis, but we must also take responsibility for building climate-resilient economies.”

a5792.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5792.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5792.title: President of Ghana
a5792.speech: Expressed optimism about Africa’s place in a multipolar world, noting that with a young and rapidly growing population, Africa has the potential to be a key driver of global trade and innovation: “Trade in Africa is growing exponentially. We have the human resources and the market size to be a major player in the global economy. The challenge is ensuring that African nations cooperate strategically to maximize our collective strength” ; called for stronger regional partnerships and policies that promote fair trade, industrialization, and economic integration under frameworks like the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

a5883.speaker: The White House
a5883.name: The White House
a5883.speech: Announced last night that President Trump has suspended the military assistance the United States government was giving to Ukraine.

a5883.speaker: Senior White House official (anonymous)
a5883.name: Senior White House official (anonymous)
a5883.speech: Told VOA in an email that "President Trump has made clear that he is focusing on peace. He added that they want America's allies to place emphasis on that matter." ; Said the Trump administration suspended the weapons assistance to Ukraine so that a review of American aid could be carried out, to verify that it is contributing to a solution.

a5883.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5883.name: Donald Trump
a5883.title: US President
a5883.speech: Said on Monday that the rare earth minerals agreement with Ukraine is important for the continuation of the assistance the United States gives to Ukraine, and indicated he would give further details in his awaited address to both houses of the U.S. Congress; has pushed for the war between Ukraine and Russia to be brought to a swift end.

a5883.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukrainian President
a5883.name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
a5883.title: Ukrainian President
a5883.speech: Expressed fear that Trump's solution for stopping the war would hand Russia a victory.

a6015.speaker: Official figures
a6015.name: Official figures
a6015.speech: Estimate that more than 50,000 people have been displaced.

a6015.speaker: Doctors Without Borders / Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
a6015.name: Doctors Without Borders / Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
a6015.speech: Has launched an emergency response in two temporary resettlement centres, and is urgently calling for a coordinated and sustained humanitarian effort in locations facing a surge in needs due to the latest displacement.

a6015.speaker: Sebastian Traficante, MSF head of operations in Mozambique
a6015.name: Sebastian Traficante
a6015.title: MSF head of operations in Mozambique
a6015.speech: "This crisis cannot remain invisible. The impact of violence shouldn't be normalised. More lives will be at risk, and the health and dignity of thousands will continue to deteriorate. People need a coordinated, long-term humanitarian commitment that guarantees access to healthcare and basic services for all."

a6015.speaker: Rosalina Maciel, displaced woman from the village of Ocua
a6015.name: Rosalina Maciel
a6015.title: displaced woman from the village of Ocua
a6015.speech: "When the attack happened, I was preparing my harvest for sale. Then we heard gunshots, and everyone started running. Now, my entire village is gone, everything is ashes. We're registered here [at the resettlement camp], but we still haven't received our food. My body is sore from sleeping on the ground, waiting. As soon as I get my food, I'll go back to my machamba [a small plantation camp]. What else can I do? This conflict feels endless."

a6015.speaker: MSF teams
a6015.name: MSF teams
a6015.speech: Have found that the most common symptoms among adults in temporary centres are anxiety and hunger.

a6015.speaker: Sebastian Traficante, MSF head of operations in Mozambique
a6015.name: Sebastian Traficante
a6015.title: MSF head of operations in Mozambique
a6015.speech: "Thanks to our financial and operational independence, MSF remains present and able to provide emergency medical care, mental health support, and other essential services. But the scale of the crisis far exceeds what any single organization can address alone, as violence and displacement drive needs to unprecedented levels."

a6246.speaker: Dan Smith, Maryland resident and son of a former federal worker
a6246.name: Dan Smith
a6246.title: Maryland resident and son of a former federal worker
a6246.speech: Emphasised the need for pushback: “It’s one thing to downsize the government. It’s another to try to obliterate it. And that’s what’s happening. It’s frightening and disgusting and requires pushback.”

a6246.speaker: Dante O’Hara, federal worker
a6246.name: Dante O’Hara
a6246.title: federal worker
a6246.speech: Expressed concern over rising racial tensions: “As a Black worker, these attacks on diversity and inclusion feel like a Jim Crow 2.0 — re-segregating the workforce.”

a6246.speaker: Democrats
a6246.name: Democrats
a6246.speech: Worry about Musk’s unchecked power and potential legal violations, raising concerns about democratic governance and federal integrity.

a6370.speaker: Associated Press
a6370.name: Associated Press
a6370.speech: Reported, among other outlets, that a federal judge on Friday dealt Trump and his billionaire ally Elon Musk their first major setback in the dismantling of USAID, ordering a temporary halt to plans to remove thousands of the agency's employees from duty.

a6370.speaker: Carl Nichols, US District Judge (Trump appointee)
a6370.name: Carl Nichols
a6370.title: US District Judge (Trump appointee)
a6370.speech: Ordered a temporary halt to the plans to remove thousands of USAID employees from duty; also agreed to block an order that would have given USAID employees overseas only 30 days to return to the US with their families at government expense, and ordered that employees already placed on leave be reinstated ; but rejected a request by two federal employee unions for a temporary block on the funds frozen by the Trump administration until further hearings on the employees' lawsuit take place.

a6370.speaker: Nature (magazine)
a6370.name: Nature (magazine)
a6370.speech: Reports that the loss of USAID could lead in Africa to an interruption of emergency responses to outbreaks such as mpox and the Marburg virus; training programmes accelerated since the COVID-19 pandemic could slow down; HIV/AIDS testing, treatment and prevention programmes as well as immunisation initiatives would be affected ; reports that the US decisions - the freezing of foreign aid and the withdrawal from the WHO in Geneva - would affect billions of dollars in annual funding to fight HIV, malaria and other areas of global health, and that more than 20 million people, mainly in Africa, including more than a million children and pregnant women, receive antiretroviral medicines under the 6.5 billion dollar PEPFAR programme.

a6370.speaker: Researchers (cited by Nature)
a6370.name: Researchers (cited by Nature)
a6370.speech: Say that this will cost lives and threaten global security.

a6370.speaker: Peter Horby, infectious disease researcher at the University of Oxford, Britain
a6370.name: Peter Horby
a6370.title: infectious disease researcher at the University of Oxford, Britain
a6370.speech: "The world will become less safe as a result."

a6370.speaker: The Conversation
a6370.name: The Conversation
a6370.speech: From 2000 to 2021 USAID's work helped prevent 7.6 million deaths from malaria; USAID's work on the development and introduction of the malaria vaccine, seen as a turning point in the fight against the disease, would now also be called into question.

a6370.speaker: HIV researcher in Africa (anonymous, runs a PEPFAR-supported clinic, not named for fear of reprisals)
a6370.name: HIV researcher in Africa (anonymous
a6370.title: runs a PEPFAR-supported clinic, not named for fear of reprisals)
a6370.speech: "There is chaos."

a6370.speaker: Salim Abdool Karim, director of the centre for the AIDS research programme in South Africa, Durban
a6370.name: Salim Abdool Karim
a6370.title: director of the centre for the AIDS research programme in South Africa, Durban
a6370.speech: "People had no chance to find alternative sources of funding, because the matter came so suddenly."

a6370.speaker: Salim Abdool Karim, director of the centre for the AIDS research programme in South Africa, Durban
a6370.name: Salim Abdool Karim
a6370.title: director of the centre for the AIDS research programme in South Africa, Durban
a6370.speech: Hopes that in South Africa, where the government carries out the bulk of HIV treatment with the help of PEPFAR funds, the effects of a possible dissolution of the agency would be minimal, but that in many other African countries "the effects would be catastrophic if PEPFAR services were discontinued. Governments cannot simply step in to close the gap."

a6370.speaker: Natasha Lindstaedt, professor in the department of government at the University of Essex (in The Conversation)
a6370.name: Natasha Lindstaedt
a6370.title: professor in the department of government at the University of Essex (in The Conversation)
a6370.speech: Reports that although the Trump administration granted an exemption for the continuation of "life-saving humanitarian assistance", including the programme giving 20 million people with HIV/AIDS access to antiretroviral medicines, the future of PEPFAR is nevertheless in question.

a6370.speaker: Natasha Lindstaedt, professor in the department of government at the University of Essex
a6370.name: Natasha Lindstaedt
a6370.title: professor in the department of government at the University of Essex
a6370.speech: "What Trump's team misunderstands is that USAID's work is also indispensable for safeguarding American interests." ; "China, which since 2013 has invested more than a trillion US dollars in infrastructure projects in Asia, Africa, Europe and Latin America, is now being given the opportunity to exert more influence worldwide. The gap in US aid is a gift to China in the battle for soft power."

a6370.speaker: Morgan Morris, journalist (in Nature magazine)
a6370.name: Morgan Morris
a6370.title: journalist (in Nature magazine)
a6370.speech: Reported that in South Africa it took only a few days for the effects of Trump's executive orders to become noticeable, with reports already of HIV clinics closing, planned training programmes being cancelled and trans health centres closing.

a6370.speaker: Tagesschau
a6370.name: Tagesschau
a6370.speech: Reported that according to Trump's original plans the agency was to be massively wound down starting at the weekend.

a6370.speaker: Union representative (anonymous)
a6370.name: Union representative (anonymous)
a6370.speech: Confirmed the figures from US media reports that the administration wanted to reduce staff from more than 10,000 to just under 300.

a6370.speaker: NPR (broadcaster)
a6370.name: NPR (broadcaster)
a6370.speech: Reported that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had been presented with a list of around 600 employees whose work worldwide was deemed essential, but that Rubio exempted fewer than 300 from being placed on leave.

a6370.speaker: Elon Musk
a6370.name: Elon Musk
a6370.speech: Called USAID a "nest of vipers of radical-left Marxists who hate America."

a6370.speaker: Fox News
a6370.name: Fox News
a6370.speech: Claimed that allegations had been come across that the agency had allegedly funded terrorist organisations and Chinese groups.

a6370.speaker: Mark Moyar, former USAID employee (on Fox News)
a6370.name: Mark Moyar
a6370.title: former USAID employee (on Fox News)
a6370.speech: Claimed that the staff had been intent on "undermining the president's will on policy questions" and on sending taxpayer money abroad in order to promote DEI and LGBT initiatives.

a6370.speaker: Opponents of Trump's policies
a6370.name: Opponents of Trump's policies
a6370.speech: Point out that these corruption allegations largely appear to lack any factual basis.

a6370.speaker: White House
a6370.name: White House
a6370.speech: Had claimed that USAID used more than eight million dollars to support the media organisation Politico.

a6370.speaker: Washington Post
a6370.name: Washington Post
a6370.speech: Showed that records prove only 44,000 USD went from USAID to Politico.

a6370.speaker: Andy Kim, US Senator from New Jersey (to CNN)
a6370.name: Andy Kim
a6370.title: US Senator from New Jersey (to CNN)
a6370.speech: Said that a dissolution of USAID would not only mean the end of life-saving global health programmes, early warning systems and food security efforts, but would also open a gap into which other countries can step. "Trump's actions weaken the global leadership role and influence of the US at a time when we are confronted with serious national security threats." ; "Trump is opening the door to our competitors and adversaries."

a6370.speaker: George Ingram, Senior Fellow at the Brookings Institution and former USAID official under the Clinton administration (to CNN)
a6370.name: George Ingram
a6370.title: Senior Fellow at the Brookings Institution and former USAID official under the Clinton administration (to CNN)
a6370.speech: Says USAID is not only altruistic but also serves national interests: the agency can develop markets with which the US can trade, and had also helped make countries more stable, which in turn could curb global migration and prevent the US from being drawn into conflicts overseas.

a6370.speaker: Gillian Caldwell, former USAID climate officer (to CNN)
a6370.name: Gillian Caldwell
a6370.title: former USAID climate officer (to CNN)
a6370.speech: Said USAID's climate programmes had fought energy poverty but had also created a level playing field for US companies in the field of renewable energy.

a6370.speaker: Angela Apeagyei, assistant professor at the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME), University of Washington, and author of a study on health spending in sub-Saharan Africa in 2024
a6370.name: Angela Apeagyei
a6370.title: assistant professor at the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME), University of Washington, and author of a study on health spending in sub-Saharan Africa in 2024
a6370.speech: African countries must ultimately become more independent of external donors and "give priority to domestic financing of the health sector and to efficient management of public finances."

a6370.speaker: Walters Kamaya, Namibian ministry spokesperson
a6370.name: Walters Kamaya
a6370.title: Namibian ministry spokesperson
a6370.speech: Affirmed that Namibia will continue its health measures despite the loss of US aid, stressing that USAID funding represents merely a supplementary resource and must be regarded as such. "With or without USAID, we will continue to provide health services for our people. Of course the loss will be felt, but that cannot be an excuse for failing."

a6385.speaker: Crusivia Hichikumba, Permanent Secretary for Investment and Industrialisation, Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry, Zambia
a6385.name: Crusivia Hichikumba
a6385.title: Permanent Secretary for Investment and Industrialisation, Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry, Zambia
a6385.speech: Explained that the agreement was a testament to the shared commitment to creating an ecosystem where businesses could thrive ; speaking at the signing ceremony, noted that this was also aimed at creating an environment for businesses to innovate, and contribute to the nation's economic development.

a6385.speaker: Crusivia Hichikumba, Permanent Secretary for Investment and Industrialisation, Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry, Zambia
a6385.name: Crusivia Hichikumba
a6385.title: Permanent Secretary for Investment and Industrialisation, Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry, Zambia
a6385.speech: “As you may be aware, the Ministry of Commerce, Trade, and Industry is charged with the responsibility for formulating and implementing policies aimed at creating a conducive business environment for private sector growth,” he said ; said the ministry was dedicated to driving economic progress through strategic collaborations and initiatives that support the private sector ; said the government recognises that a robust and dynamic private sector is crucial for job creation, innovation, and sustainable economic growth ; however said achieving this required an enabling environment where businesses can operate efficiently, access essential resources, and navigate regulatory frameworks with ease.

a6385.speaker: Crusivia Hichikumba, Permanent Secretary for Investment and Industrialisation, Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry, Zambia
a6385.name: Crusivia Hichikumba
a6385.title: Permanent Secretary for Investment and Industrialisation, Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry, Zambia
a6385.speech: “The USAID Business Enabling Project has been a steadfast partner in our journey towards achieving these goals,” he said ; noted that the USAID Business Enabling Project brings a wealth of knowledge and experience that will be invaluable in the government efforts to create a more competitive and inclusive economy.

a6385.speaker: Crusivia Hichikumba, Permanent Secretary for Investment and Industrialisation, Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry, Zambia
a6385.name: Crusivia Hichikumba
a6385.title: Permanent Secretary for Investment and Industrialisation, Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry, Zambia
a6385.speech: Added that through the agreement, the government was establishing a framework for implementing programmes that would address key challenges faced by our business community ; said the programmes would focus on streamlining regulatory processes as well as fostering innovation and entrepreneurship ; “This collaboration is also a reflection of our commitment to aligning with international best practices and leveraging global expertise to address local challenges,” he said.

a6392.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6392.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6392.speech: According to the WHO, the most affected countries are Zambia and Zimbabwe, while Mozambique, Tanzania, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia and Nigeria have recorded active cholera outbreaks, with a total of 26,000 cases and 700 deaths.

a6392.speaker: Fiona Braka, emergency manager of the WHO Regional Office for Africa
a6392.name: Fiona Braka
a6392.title: emergency manager of the WHO Regional Office for Africa
a6392.speech: “Climate change and conflicts are fuelling the fire. Floods, cyclones and droughts reduce access to drinking water and create an ideal environment for cholera to develop,” she explained by teleconference from Brazzaville.

a6392.speaker: Fiona Braka, emergency manager of the WHO Regional Office for Africa
a6392.name: Fiona Braka
a6392.title: emergency manager of the WHO Regional Office for Africa
a6392.speech: Said that these vaccination campaigns represent an important effort in which the WHO is collaborating, because international stocks of cholera vaccines are scarce ; for that reason, also considered that solutions should be examined that include better access to drinking water, hygiene and sanitation facilities, as well as quality diagnosis and treatment.

a6392.speaker: National Directorate of Public Health of Mozambique (bulletin on the progression of the disease)
a6392.name: National Directorate of Public Health of Mozambique (bulletin on the progression of the disease)
a6392.speech: According to the most recent bulletin, with data up to 31 January, a cumulative total of 10,859 cholera cases had been recorded since 1 October 2023.

a6392.speaker: United Kingdom
a6392.name: United Kingdom
a6392.speech: Announced a humanitarian aid package of 100 million pounds (117 million euros) for Ethiopia; the programme aims to give more than three million Ethiopians, mostly women and children, access to health services, in particular to combat malnutrition and outbreaks of malaria and cholera.

a6392.speaker: European Commission
a6392.name: European Commission
a6392.speech: Has also spoken out regarding the cholera outbreaks and will help, with one million euros, to fight the epidemic in Zambia, which could affect 3.5 million people.

a6620.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB, 2025 Country Focus report)
a6620.name: African Development Bank (AfDB
a6620.title: 2025 Country Focus report)
a6620.speech: Has projected that Malawi's actual grant disbursements will fall short by 61.8 percent of the target in the 2025/26 financial year following aid cuts and US tariff impositions, compounded by the suspension of $350 million annual funding from USAID, the cancellation of the $350 million five-year Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) land compact and the imposition of an 18 percent tariff on exports from Malawi to the US. "While the first-round trade effects of the tariffs are limited due to the small share of Malawi's exports to the US at [less than four percent], the aid cuts will have a big effect given that 87 percent of aid is allocated to capital projects, directly affecting infrastructure development and economic growth. The second-round trade effects emanate from reduced global growth, especially that of South Africa, the European Union and the United Kingdom, which will reduce Malawi's export demand." ; AfDB observed that in the medium-to-long-term, both aid cuts and tariff imposition will have employment, productivity and competitiveness and growth effects that will exacerbate macro-fiscal instability. ; AfDB data further show that while domestic revenue has risen from 14.7 percent of GDP in 2022 to 18.1 percent of GDP in 2024, expenditures have risen from 26.8 percent of GDP in 2022 to 32 percent of GDP in 2024 in the face of a rising financing gap of about $3.59 billion or $0.63 billion annually.

a6620.speaker: Agnes Nyirongo, Centre for Social Concern economic governance officer
a6620.name: Agnes Nyirongo
a6620.title: Centre for Social Concern economic governance officer
a6620.speech: In an interview, observed that the sharp decline in disbursements has left a substantial funding gap, undermining the government's ability to meet its obligations. She said: "Grant financing is predominantly allocated to capital projects such as infrastructure development, healthcare systems, education facilities, agricultural support programs, and public works. The loss of this funding means delays or outright cancellation of projects, threatening employment, productivity and service delivery. Many initiatives tied to long-term growth are now hanging in the balance."

a6620.speaker: Simplex Chithyola-Banda, Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a6620.name: Simplex Chithyola-Banda
a6620.title: Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a6620.speech: Projected grants at K1.17 trillion in the 2024/25 fiscal year, with K1.1 trillion expected from international organisations and K72.69 billion from foreign governments.

a6620.speaker: Williams Banda, Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs spokesperson
a6620.name: Williams Banda
a6620.title: Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs spokesperson
a6620.speech: Was yet to respond to our questionnaire, but is quoted as having said that only K9.2 billion of USAid funding appeared in the 2024/25 National Budget, but that the US government off-budget projection in the 2024/25 fiscal year was about K307 billion.

a6620.speaker: Jacob Hara, Minister of Transport
a6620.name: Jacob Hara
a6620.title: Minister of Transport
a6620.speech: In his earlier comment following the cancellation of MCC, said the compact came with funding for ongoing road works. "We shall have to start from scratch looking for new financing," he said.

a6644.speaker: Burnnet Khulumbo, Care Malawi humanitarian assistance programmes manager
a6644.name: Burnnet Khulumbo
a6644.title: Care Malawi humanitarian assistance programmes manager
a6644.speech: Says the flood trigger statement and anticipatory action plan will help to avert the impact of disasters in Nsanje and Chikwawa districts ; said the initiative seeks to enable partners to take proactive steps ahead of predicted hazards, preventing or reducing acute humanitarian impacts before they fully unfold ; "Floods remain one of the most recurrent and devastating hazards in Malawi, particularly in the Shire Valley. Therefore, this workshop will review and validate the flood trigger statement, which specifies the forecast thresholds that will activate anticipatory actions."

a6644.speaker: Zione Viyazyi, Department of Disaster Management Affairs principal disaster preparedness officer
a6644.name: Zione Viyazyi
a6644.title: Department of Disaster Management Affairs principal disaster preparedness officer
a6644.speech: Said there are no major gaps currently but there is need for more localised forecasting capacity to trigger area-specific early actions for councils such as Nsanje, Chikwawa and Phalombe ; "We have made a good progress at the national level in piloting and integrating anticipatory action into disaster risk reduction efforts. A National Anticipatory Action Framework was drafted to institutionalise the anticipatory action into national policy."

a6644.speaker: Michael Mwale, Churches Aid in Relief and Development (Card) resilience officer
a6644.name: Michael Mwale
a6644.title: Churches Aid in Relief and Development (Card) resilience officer
a6644.speech: Said it was time the country moved from preparing for disasters at the higher level to involving the grassroots ; "We expect this workshop to help stakeholders finalise a trigger statement and action plan ready for operationalisation."

a6657.speaker: Bio Baguiri Seydou, director of the "Access to Land" project (MCA-Benin), representing the coordinator
a6657.name: Bio Baguiri Seydou
a6657.title: director of the "Access to Land" project (MCA-Benin), representing the coordinator
a6657.speech: In his welcoming remarks, stated that through these installations he intends to strengthen the geodetic, topographic and cartographic capacities of the country by equipping it with modern instruments to combat land insecurity; presented the technical improvements to be made to the process of establishing rural land plans (PFR) and of converting occupancy permits into land titles; clarified that with GPS, measurements taken in the field now undergo differential correction in post-processing to increase precision; explained that MCA-Benin's objective through the project is to put an end to the multiple systems used until now and to have a single reference system in the country; and said that during the four days participants will take part in the acquisition of aerial data by a remote-controlled drone, learn techniques for determining quality control points for ortho-images and take part in group work on geodetic, cartographic and cadastral themes.

a6657.speaker: Randy Wood, deputy resident director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation
a6657.name: Randy Wood
a6657.title: deputy resident director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation
a6657.speech: Returned to the objectives of the "Access to Land" project, whose implementation provides for the production of 300 rural land plan titles in some forty rural communes of Benin as well as the conversion of 30,000 presumed ownership documents into land titles; acknowledged the support and collaboration of the Beninese government; and urged the participants to follow attentively the various modules that will be presented.

a6657.speaker: Didier Sacramento, deputy chief of staff of the Ministry of Urban Planning of Benin
a6657.name: Didier Sacramento
a6657.title: deputy chief of staff of the Ministry of Urban Planning of Benin
a6657.speech: In his opening remarks, said this workshop comes to settle the many problems linked to land management in the country and urged the participants to give much more attention to this training in order to find adequate solutions to land problems; said the government's expectation is to see the largest possible number of specialists trained in the use of permanent stations and mobile receivers in mapping and the land registry.

a6951.speaker: Dr. Philip Mpango, Vice President of the United Republic of Tanzania
a6951.name: Dr. Philip Mpango
a6951.title: Vice President of the United Republic of Tanzania
a6951.speech: Said Tanzania emphasizes the importance of sustainable financing mechanisms to ensure resilience in responding to public health emergencies in Africa, and said Tanzania is determined to increase domestic resource mobilization, strengthen innovative financing solutions, as well as support regional initiatives that reduce dependence on foreign aid, thereby ensuring that Africa's health priorities are addressed by African governments.

a6951.speaker: Dr. Philip Mpango, Vice President of the United Republic of Tanzania
a6951.name: Dr. Philip Mpango
a6951.title: Vice President of the United Republic of Tanzania
a6951.speech: Said domestic production of diagnostic equipment, treatment, and other essential medical products is essential for self-reliance in the health sector ; "Tanzania encourages investment in local industries, a common regulatory authority across the continent, and technology transfer partnerships to strengthen Africa's capacity to respond to current and future health challenges."

a6951.speaker: Dr. Philip Mpango, Vice President of the United Republic of Tanzania
a6951.name: Dr. Philip Mpango
a6951.title: Vice President of the United Republic of Tanzania
a6951.speech: Said recent experiences with infectious disease outbreaks, including Marburg and other infectious pathogens, have highlighted the need for strong preparedness and response systems ; "Tanzania supports the development of infectious disease treatment units, rapid deployment of emergency teams, and investment in human and health infrastructure." ; stressed the importance of strengthening all pillars of public health emergencies, including disease surveillance, laboratories, infection control, equipment, and coordination for timely and effective response to outbreaks.

a6951.speaker: Dr. Philip Mpango, Vice President of the United Republic of Tanzania
a6951.name: Dr. Philip Mpango
a6951.title: Vice President of the United Republic of Tanzania
a6951.speech: Called for enhanced cooperation among African Union Member States, regional economic communities, and the Africa Centers for Disease Control to have a unified approach to responding to health emergencies, and said collaboration on research, policy, and joint capacity building plans will strengthen the collective ability to prevent, detect, and respond to emerging health threats.

a6975.speaker: USAspending.gov (official US government data)
a6975.name: USAspending.gov (official US government data)
a6975.speech: According to official data published on the USAspending.gov website, 100% of USAID-funded projects in Guinea for the year 2025 have been cancelled - in all 12 projects representing 30.76 million dollars in aid completely eliminated.

a6975.speaker: Franceinfo and Jeune Afrique (media reports)
a6975.name: Franceinfo and Jeune Afrique (media reports)
a6975.speech: According to Franceinfo and Jeune Afrique, dozens of countries around the world, notably in Africa, are undergoing severe cuts, but only a few countries, including Guinea, see all of their funding completely eliminated.
