a6977.speaker: UN General Assembly draft resolution
a6977.name: UN General Assembly draft resolution
a6977.speech: Calls for "an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire" in Gaza, seeks "the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages," and demands "immediate access" to widespread humanitarian aid for the citizens of Gaza ; seeks to address "the need for accountability" by asking UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres to present "proposals on how the United Nations could help to advance accountability."

a6977.speaker: Earlier draft resolution (seen by AFP)
a6977.name: Earlier draft resolution (seen by AFP)
a6977.speech: Aimed to establish an international mechanism to help investigate and prosecute those who are responsible for violating international law against the Palestinians, but that language was not included in the draft resolution that will be put to a vote.

a6977.speaker: Second draft UN General Assembly resolution
a6977.name: Second draft UN General Assembly resolution
a6977.speech: Will call on Israel to respect the mandate of UNRWA and allow it to continue its "safe and unhindered humanitarian assistance" operations, after Israel voted to ban it.

a6977.speaker: Riyad Mansour, Palestinian UN ambassador
a6977.name: Riyad Mansour
a6977.title: Palestinian UN ambassador
a6977.speech: "Gaza today is the bleeding heart of Palestine" ; "The images of our children burning in tents, with no food in their bellies and no hopes and no horizon for the future, and after having endured pain and loss for more than a year, should haunt the conscience of the world and prompt action to end this nightmare," calling for an end to the "impunity."

a6977.speaker: Danny Danon, Israeli UN ambassador
a6977.name: Danny Danon
a6977.title: Israeli UN ambassador
a6977.speech: Denounced the draft resolution ahead of the vote: "If you truly want peace, it begins with dismantling this infrastructure of hate and the glorification of terror," in reference to humanitarian agency UNRWA, whose employees were accused by Israel of assisting with the October 7 attacks.

a6977.speaker: AFP tally based on official data
a6977.name: AFP tally based on official data
a6977.speech: Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack resulted in the deaths of 1,208 people, mostly civilians, a count that includes hostages who died or were killed while being held in Gaza.

a6977.speaker: Hamas-run health ministry (data considered reliable by the UN)
a6977.name: Hamas-run health ministry (data considered reliable by the UN)
a6977.speech: Israel's retaliatory offensive in Gaza has killed at least 44,786 people, mostly civilians.

a6977.speaker: Israeli military
a6977.name: Israeli military
a6977.speech: Says that of the 96 hostages who remain in Gaza, 34 are dead.

a7140.speaker: UNICEF (United Nations children's agency)
a7140.name: UNICEF (United Nations children's agency)
a7140.speech: Said on Friday it will run out of its supply of lifesaving food to treat children suffering from acute forms of malnutrition in Ethiopia and Nigeria within the next two months due to lack of funding exacerbated by Trump administration cuts to foreign aid ; says some 1.3 million children under five suffering from severe acute malnutrition risk losing access to lifesaving support this year in Ethiopia and Nigeria ; said that in Nigeria it may run out of supplies to feed 80,000 malnourished children as soon as the end of this month ; according to UNICEF, twenty-three mobile health clinics were taken out of operation in the region of Afar, with only seven left operating due to funding cuts.

a7140.speaker: Van der Heijden, UNICEF official
a7140.name: Van der Heijden
a7140.title: UNICEF official
a7140.speech: Described recently being in a hospital in Maiduguri with a child who was so malnourished that her skin was falling off ; "This funding crisis will become a child survival crisis," warned Van der Heijden, adding that the sudden nature of the cuts did not give the agency the ability to mitigate the risks.

a7385.speaker: Dr Leila Mansoor, senior scientist with the Caprisa Matrix project, University of KwaZulu-Natal
a7385.name: Dr Leila Mansoor
a7385.title: senior scientist with the Caprisa Matrix project, University of KwaZulu-Natal
a7385.speech: "Our participants are now very confused; we have built a relationship of trust with our communities over the years. How do we explain that the decision is based not on science but on politics?" ; Said that although the first studies have been completed they are not allowed to finalise the data analysis and provide feedback to participants and the scientific community: "Everything is now up in the air."

a7385.speaker: Tendani Tsedu, South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC) spokesperson
a7385.name: Tendani Tsedu
a7385.title: South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC) spokesperson
a7385.speech: "The Brilliant Consortium, led by the SAMRC received formal communication from USAID that our work is halted until further notice."

a7385.speaker: USAID Southern Africa (Facebook post)
a7385.name: USAID Southern Africa (Facebook post)
a7385.speech: According to a post on USAID Southern Africa's Facebook page, they have already invested $94 million (around R1.7 billion) in TB programmes run in South Africa.

a7385.speaker: Academic (anonymous, fearing it might jeopardise future funding)
a7385.name: Academic (anonymous
a7385.title: fearing it might jeopardise future funding)
a7385.speech: "Ten years of work will go to waste if our programmes (on HIV/Aids and TB, among others) have to pause for a few months." ; "It will take us years to catch up again." ; Points out the international contribution of researchers from South Africa: "Some of the most important research work on Covid-19 came from South Africa." ; "The Americans might think they don't benefit directly (from research on diseases like HIV/Aids and TB), but some diseases more common in developing countries also appear elsewhere." ; Said South Africans must find other ways to help finance their work, but it would have made a huge difference if the process occurred in phases.

a7385.speaker: The Guardian (report)
a7385.name: The Guardian (report)
a7385.speech: Reports that Kansas is currently experiencing one of the largest TB outbreaks ever recorded in the US, with 384 patients being monitored and treated there.

a7385.speaker: Another researcher (anonymous)
a7385.name: Another researcher (anonymous)
a7385.speech: Points to the ethical dilemma they are facing: "You cannot just stop programmes; there are ethical guidelines and contracts on how to work with participants and scientific data, for example."

a7385.speaker: Foster Mohale, spokesperson for the South African department of health
a7385.name: Foster Mohale
a7385.title: spokesperson for the South African department of health
a7385.speech: Says they are looking at ways in which the government can help affected research programmes. "However, it also depends on the American government's final decisions after the 90-day ban."

a7385.speaker: Elon Musk, head of Trump's newly established department of government efficiency (posts on X)
a7385.name: Elon Musk
a7385.title: head of Trump's newly established department of government efficiency (posts on X)
a7385.speech: Posted dozens of messages on X last week, calling USAID an "irreparable, criminal organisation"; accuses USAID of funding terrorism, among other things, and supporting programmes for gay and transgender people, which do not align with Trump's vision.

a7385.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7385.name: Donald Trump
a7385.title: US President
a7385.speech: Said last week that "terrible things are happening in South Africa, and the leadership is doing awful things," halting all aid funds while investigating the country, and specifically referred to the legislation on land expropriation.
